Chakra-geddon plays like an old handheld: a d-pad, an A button to confirm and a B button to go back. It works with a keyboard, a touch screen or a gamepad, and you can switch between them whenever you like.

Chakra-geddon runs in your web browser, on a phone or a computer. There is nothing to download and no account to make. Once it has loaded, it keeps working offline, so it is happy on a beach with no signal.

Open Options from the title screen, or during play from the Fanny Pack: MENU › System › Options. Change a setting with A, or with left and right. A short explanation of the setting under the cursor is shown at the bottom of the screen.

An Astral is what a state of mind looks like when it gets loose30 AM. There are 41 of them at the festival. Some live in the incense, some only come out at night, during a particular set, or when you are high enough to see them. A few are one of a kind.
You do not catch Astrals here. You bag them: wear a wild one down in battle, then "stabilise" it in a bag. That is how you make friends at this festival.
Nobody at this festival fights with fists any more. Too much effort. Conflicts are settled on the astral plane, one Astral against one Astral, taking turns.
Chai Tents
It is an infinite seven-day festival, so something is always playing somewhere. Once you know the timetable, you can be in the right place at the right time.
"Out here everything gets you a little high: every fight, every snack, the air."

Everything you carry lives in your Stash Tin (the bag page of the Fanny Pack). You start with Rs 300, a warm coconut water and a glowing blotter. Rupees come from beating trainers, finishing quests, and selling things you do not need.
"I read past lives. Only for Astrals, though. People's past lives are all Cleopatra. It got boring."

Your backpack is gone. What you have instead is a fanny pack, and it holds everything: your Astrals, your stuff, your notes and your sense of direction. Press MENU (M or Tab on a keyboard, Start on a gamepad) to open it, and MENU or B to close it.
A satire. Hydrate. Look after each other. And also:

The festival stretches along the coast from Anjuna to Arambol: beaches, stages, jungle shortcuts, a flea market, a sacred cow in the middle of the road, and eventually a temple. Most of it you cover on foot, which is fine, because nobody here is going anywhere in particular anyway.

To get your passport back from the VIP Shaman Council, you need all eight Wristbands of Enlightenment. Each one is handed over by a stage boss after you beat them, and each one (bar the last) unlocks a field technique: a way past something that blocked your path. So the bosses are also the keys to the map.

You wake up on a beach in Goa. Your passport is gone, your phone is dead, and a man with a beard like a mangrove is asking how you feel. The festival has been going on for longer than anyone can remember, and the creatures dancing in the incense are not, strictly speaking, real. They are Astrals, and you are going to need some. Chakra-geddon is a satirical creature-collecting RPG that runs in your browser, on phones and on PC. Catch Astrals, win eight wristbands from the festival's DJs, gurus and influencers, foil Team Undercover's plan to sell the sunset, dance your way down the Last Dancefloor and climb the Mainstage Temple to face the VIP Shaman Council. The game is free and runs at gioleppe.github.io/chakrageddon. It works offline once it has loaded, and you can add it to your home screen like an app. A word before you go Chakra-geddon is a satire of festival culture. In the game, getting high changes what you see and how you fight. In real life, look after yourself and each other: drink water, know what you are taking, and find the welfare tent.

Getting started: opening the game, saving, controls and options. How to play: every system in the game, explained. Walkthrough: the main story from the beach to the Council, then the postgame. Reference: side quests, legendaries, the full Astral Journal, trainers, item locations and places. Gallery: screenshots from all over the festival. Changelog: the history of the game, version by version.

Every version of Chakra-geddon since the first release, newest first. The game updates itself in your browser, so the version on the title screen is the one described at the top of this page. Highlights 1.0.0: the first release: eight Wristbands, 36 Astrals, the Mainstage Temple and the VIP Shaman Council, playable on phone and PC and installable for offline play. 1.0.4 to 1.0.20: a new opening dream, intoxication with real stakes, a goal and route hints, interiors, side quests and the Quests tab, and a drawn festival map with tuk-tuk travel. 1.0.41: a pixel cutscene for every boss, the Four, the rival and the Council. 1.0.46: being high changes the world: hallucinations, places that exist only with your ego gone, and two new Astrals. 1.0.47 and 1.0.48: the festival timetable, and boss fights with arrivals, half-health moments, their own stages and a wristband ceremony. 1.1.0: music that behaves, and sleeping until the set you want. 1.2.0: Astrals grow by chance, moves cost more water, and a Difficulty setting. 1.2.3: The Unfinished Mandala, a quest for Mandalord. 1.2.5: three new routes (Fishermen's Cove, the Load-In Road and the Last Dancefloor) and the Mainstage Temple rebuilt as a ziggurat. 1.3.0: the manual and walkthrough go online, with a round of fixes it turned up. 1.4.0: the whole game in Italian, with a language switch on the title and in Options. 1.4.1: menus that wrap round, Astrals that come in and go back in battle, and incense you wade through.

New Menus wrap round. Press down on the last row to come back to the top, up on the first to reach the bottom; in the battle menu and the move list, left and right wrap round too. Astrals come in and go back. Yours and every trainer's arrive as a point of light that bursts open, the creature growing out of it; a wild one shimmers out of the haze. Swapped out, an Astral turns to light and streaks back to its owner before the next one comes in. Wading through incense. Clouds of incense billow when you step into them and wrap round your feet while you stand in them, like tall grass; dark bushes shake. With Reduced motion on, nothing moves.

New Italiano. The whole game is translated: dialogue, menus, battles, quests, names and the credits. Pick the language with Language on the title screen or at the top of Options; the game uses your browser's language the first time. The page restarts when you switch (your progress is saved first). The game can take more languages: they are plain dictionary files, one per language.

New The Chakra-geddon manual: a user manual, a full walkthrough, reference pages and this changelog, online at gioleppe.github.io/chakrageddon-manual. Changed Sergeant Baksheesh brings a stronger team (Lv 33 to 35, five Astrals). He only turns up after the third memo, which is behind Baba Smoke, and his old team was far too weak by then. He pays more, too. Dreamer now dodges exactly what it says: one attack in seven (it was a little more). Fixed The hidden Masala Chai on the Last Dancefloor was under Darkpsy Superfan Vlad, where nobody could reach it. It is in the clearing beside him now. The Mainstage Temple's sign, the Water Auntie, Chai Mama, Lead Lakshmi and the Council talked about doors and floors; since the ziggurat they talk about terraces and stairs. In the Blottertot version of the last rival fight, his ace was Lv 40 instead of Lv 43 like the other two. The tuk-tuk driver at the Flea Market now tells you to ride from the Map, where the tuk-tuk actually is. Banyan's tip no longer says chai brings you down: water, a nap in a Chai Tent or a long walk do.

New Fishermen's Cove, a large new area between the beach and the Sunset Cliff: rock pools, a fishing village with a toddy shack and its own shop, a palm grove and two islets. A lifeguard lets you round the rocks once you have four Wristbands. Tides: in the cove the flats are wet sand from 4 to 10, morning and evening, and sea the rest of the time. Get caught as the tide turns and you splash back to dry sand; sit on a flat rock to wait for it. A tide table is posted on a sign. Low Tide quest: cross the flats to a sea cave and find Rosa's grandfather's boat, with a fridge-sized Lobsterlad asleep in it. Afterwards Rosa rows you up the coast to the Arabian Sea Shallows and back. The Load-In Road, the festival's service road between the Sunset Cliff and the Backstage Container: a truck park, a security checkpoint, a lighting store maze, a generator yard and a crew catering corner with a shop. Power Cut quest: get all three generators running again (a pulled cable, an empty tank and a Bottler "doing maintenance"), for a reward that includes Earplugs. The Generator Disco, an eighth set on the timetable: 21:00 to 03:00 in the truck park once the power is back, with festoon lights, lasers, a DJ and a dancing Glowkid. The Last Dancefloor, a victory road south of the Backstage: lanes of dancers that move along with every step you take, a superfan of every boss, the Front Row, wild Astrals in the packed crowd and a Chai Tent in the welfare tent. At the front of the Last Dancefloor the crowd lifts you, passes you overhead and throws you onto the stage, where the temple is revealed. The second time you get a short version. Lost in the Crowd quest: help Ziggy find Noor, who promised not to move from the light towers. The Mainstage Temple is now a terraced ziggurat, five terraces climbing into the night, each with its own look, guarded by one of the Four in order and then the rival. Nobody can be walked round. A cutscene when you first enter the temple: the terraces light up one by one with the music and the Council look down at you. Eight new trainers in the cove, eight on the Load-In Road and ten on the Last Dancefloor, plus new pickups in each. Changed The path down from the Sunset Cliff now comes out in Fishermen's Cove; climbing back up still needs the Banyan Root Climb. The Sunset Cliff's east exit and the Backstage's west exit now lead onto the Load-In Road. The back stairs at the foot of the temple bring you out at the side gate of the Last Dancefloor.

New The tuk-tuk now plays a short ride on screen (the night road, palms, a horn, you waving from the back) before you arrive. With Reduce Motion it is a single still frame. Meeting Juniper the first time plays a candlelit scene of her riffling an enormous tarot deck and turning a card. Changed Beaten members of the Four no longer vanish: each walks up and stands aside on the next floor, with a line for you. The rival does the same. Losing halfway up still puts everyone back. Sergeant Baksheesh only turns up on the Sunset Cliff after you hand in the Team Undercover memos, as the last step of Team Undercover's Plan. The hippie warns you he is coming. The Backstage Container no longer has a Chai Tent. The Green Room door is now in the north wall of the Backstage's main hall, and can only be reached from the hall. Fixed Juniper's portrait now shows her beanie and round glasses. The cliff tourist no longer talks about a man in uniform who isn't there.

New The Unfinished Mandala, a quest for Mandalord. After his fight Baba Smoke tells the story of the faded sand mandala in the Sadhu Cave and maps the four coloured sands you need: shell sand at sunrise on the beach, kumkum from the pujari, turmeric from a line cook at the Omelette Stall, and UV powder that only shows while you are Peaking. Laying the mandala sober plays a new scene: it fills in, turns, and Mandalord steps out. Once Mandalord is caught, Baba sweeps the mandala away and gives you a Sand Mala, a held item that keeps a clear head (no Thought Loops, no K-holes). Changed After losing to a boss, their cutscene plays in full again when you retry. Rematches still show the short card. Saves that had already met Mandalord pick the quest up at its last step. Fixed Waking at a Chai Tent after losing to a boss no longer keeps the boss music playing.

New The Wristbands page shows the selected band turning in fake 3D, each with its own material, plus who gave it to you, a description and what it lets you do. Bands you haven't earned show as a dark silhouette with the boss to beat.

New Ranger Asha at the top of the Sandy Trail keeps the way to the Poi Pit shut while you carry a single Astral, and hands out three baggies once. It is always open after DJ Diabolo is beaten. Two new easy trainers on the trail: Beach Bum Rick and Drummer Kofi (optional). Changed The Sandy Trail is bigger and winds: tide pools and a drum circle south of the creek, dunes and more incense to the north. The first trainers are gentler: the Juggler, the Fire Spinner and the rival bring lower-level Astrals and pay a bit more.

New Options › Difficulty: Easy (you deal 1.2x damage and take 0.8x), Normal, or Hard (you deal 0.8x and take 1.2x). Astrals now grow by chance: each level-up adds 0, 1 or 2 Hydration, and the other stats grow around the species' rate with a little luck either way. Every evolution line grows each stat early, steadily or late, and the summary says which. Changed Every move costs 1.4 times the water it did, and Astrals start with more water. Trainers' Astrals carry extra water to match. The Water Auntie in the temple now refills water any time during the Four; her full heal is still once a climb. Astrals from older saves keep their stats on the average curve.

New The Arabian Sea Shallows is now a much bigger bay with a sunbathing beach, sandbars and a rocky islet in the middle. The Sea Grotto, a cave inside the islet with tide pools, wild Astrals, two trainers and a hidden pickup. Mad Dogs and Englishmen quest: a party of sunburnt British tourists needs the cool blue clay from the grotto. It works, and they turn bright blue. New trainers on the beach and in the grotto.

New The Flea Market Back Alley, a new area between the market and the Omelette Stall. The first time in, an undercover constable pulls a shutter down behind you (a pixel cutscene) and you can't leave until all seven Team Undercover agents are beaten. Once they pack up and go, the alley fills with people getting high instead. Saves already past Chef Raju find the alley cleared.

Changed A Coconut for Lakshmi is a longer quest: beat Coconut Wallah Pradeep for a green coconut, get a Marigold Garland from Flower Seller Meena, have the pujari bless both, then offer them to Lakshmi on the road and walk her to the shrine. Fixed Props standing on a floor (the cow, lamps and shrines in the shrine courtyard) no longer show a square of the wrong ground around them.

New The Journal shows where to find each Astral you have seen: every place it lives, at what levels and under what conditions, plus what it grows from and into. The Astral stash can be sorted by order caught, name or level, and you can swap a stashed Astral with one in your party in one go.

New At a Chai Tent you can choose which set to sleep until. The night passes on a clock, and if the set is right there the camera shows you the crowd and the stage as you wake. Changed In battle, lines meant to be read (a boss's words at their big moment, your reflection, the explanations of how high you are) now wait for A. After a battle, the world's music now starts only once the battle screen has closed, with the battle song fading out first. Fixed Boss fights no longer sound like two songs at once: the chord layer that plays when you are high now matches each track's key, and a boss's cutscene and battle share one theme.

New Juniper's Past Life Readings: after your sixth Wristband, Banyan's astral body floats down to tell you a tarot reader has set up at the Flea Market. For Rs 500 she helps an Astral remember a move it has forgotten or skipped. Changed Learning a new move now shows a full page with the new move's details and a note for whichever move you are pointing at, so you can compare before replacing one. The Steel Flask now takes a third off every move's water cost, instead of 1.

New The Astral summary explains itself: point at any move, stat, type, the ability or the held item and press A for a note on what it does. Changed Kaleidoscope Spit costs 16 water instead of 10. A beaten trainer who walks away (the lost backpackers, Astra-Zero) now holds you in place until they have gone. Fixed The held item on the summary no longer runs into the panel's edge.
Changed On a phone held upright, the picture now fills the whole width of the screen.

New A System tab in the Fanny Pack with Save, Options and Unstuck. Unstuck puts you back where you entered the area. Transitions between areas: a sweep when you walk off the edge of a map, and a closing diamond at doors, rides and whiteouts.

New Hold B to run. The Dirt Road's two detours are now long areas of their own, the Jungle Shortcut and the Roadside Shrine, each with its own wild Astrals and trainers. Three small stories along them: The Lost Tour Group, Flowers Before Dawn, and A Coconut for Lakshmi (which gets the cow off the road for good). Changed Walking is a touch slower, to make room for running. Route hints now send you round the cow the right way. Fixed The camera rises while someone is talking, so the text box no longer hides you at the bottom of a map.
Changed The Four are now one climb: the temple's Chai Tent turns you away once you have started, and losing halfway puts all four back at their doors.

New Rizla papers and amber vials have their own capture animations. Changed Astra-Zero walks off after your second fight instead of vanishing. Picking a move to forget now asks for confirmation, with "No" as the default.

Changed The Clogged Dirt Road is bigger: the cow really blocks the road, and the two detours, through the jungle and through the shrine, each have grass and a trainer you can't slip past. Tuk-tuks take up 2x2 tiles and scooters 2x1, with new sprites in a range of colours. Fixed The capture fanfare now plays after the bag stops shaking, not before.

New The blotter in one press: L on the keyboard, Y on a gamepad (Quick Items moves to X), or LICK on the phone pad. It is also the first row of Quick Items. The Stash Tin can be sorted by type, by name or by quantity. Changed On seven routes a trainer now watches the crossing you have to use, so some fights can't be avoided; on six wide routes trainers look around. Trainers can see across water. Creature miniatures in the party list and on the starter card are drawn small instead of shrunk. Held items are sold one at a time, like outfits. Quest outfits lost in a whiteout can be had again from the person who gave them. No idle dancing or bored blotter licks indoors. The guesthouse has proper beds and windows, and its noticeboard hangs on the wall. Fixed The title screen shows the right version number. A few trainers no longer stare at walls. Long abilities are shown in full on the summary, and long Journal notes open a full page. The shop's Leave tab can be selected with the keys. Blottertot's eyes are easier to see, and Glowkid no longer seems to have three arms from behind.

New At a Chai Tent you can rest or check the stash; swapping Astrals with the stash only works at a tent. Move in the party menu swaps an Astral with any slot. Changed Outfits are sold one at a time and show "Sold out" while you own one. Fixed The yurt, temple and cave walls now look right from every side.

Changed Wild encounters come at a steady pace instead of being too frequent or too sparse, and being high raises them less than before. After a whiteout you wake at the last hut that took you in (a Chai Tent, a guesthouse bed or Banyan's hammock). On a boss's stage, the Chai Tent and the shops turn you away until that boss is beaten. Fixed A new wild fight no longer starts on the very first step after the last one.

New Boss arrivals: the first time you face a boss, the music drops, the crowd turns and the camera goes over to them. Every boss has a moment at half health that changes the fight, such as Diabolo dropping the track or Svetlana's chant flipping the type chart. Every boss fights on a battle stage of their own, with a theme tune of their own. A short wristband ceremony after each boss, with the crowd cheering. The bosses' stages on the map are dressed up: an LED wall and lasers in the Poi Pit, cushions and incense in the yurt, UV and fog in the forest, and a different theme for each room of the temple. After the credits, an end card sums up your festival and can be saved as a picture.

New The festival timetable: after your third Wristband, Banyan brings it to you. Seven sets run at set times around the festival, each with its own crowd, music, an Astral of its own and someone special to meet. A Sets page in the Fanny Pack shows what is on and what is next; the map marks places with a set on. A Chai Tent can let you sleep until the next set starts. DJ Diabolo only takes his rematch during his headline set. Two trainers come out only at night.

New Being high changes the world: lights glow from the Come-up, mandalas drift over the ground and performers leave trails from Peaking, and a warm pad plays under the music. With your ego gone, each area has a hallucination that dissolves as you get close, and your reflection sometimes waits to fight you. Places that only exist with your ego gone: the Inner Room in the Sadhu Cave, stairs of light off the Sunset Cliff, and an open road where the cow lies. Banyan's shack has a new diary page. About 50 people have something to say when you are high, and people hint at Astrals that only show up when you are higher. Two new Astrals: Mirrorling and Lucidra. The Journal now has 41. Fixed With reduced motion, the steady strobes no longer move.

New The Poi Pit is rebuilt: Diabolo stands on a raised stage with strobes, and a packed crowd of real dancers fills the floor. You have to cross it, past at least one trainer, to reach him. Trainers on a dancefloor dance until they spot you. Fixed Quest markers no longer bob with reduced motion.
New Stand still too long with the blotter in your bag and you lick it out of boredom. Banyan warns you about it. Changed The Quick Items tip now comes up on the Sandy Trail after your first battle.

Changed Licking the blotter several times in a row shows only the latest "how high" message. The festival tape on the beach disappears once you have an Astral, and Banyan tells you he has taken it down.

New A livelier hero: a bandana, shades pushed up, an open beach shirt, glowsticks and wristbands. Left standing, you dance to the beat. A one-time tip explains Quick Items. Fixed Trees, palms, bamboo and flags now sway with hand-drawn frames, with no more stripes.

New A pixel cutscene for every boss, Sergeant Baksheesh, the Four, the rival and the VIP Shaman Council the first time you face them. Retries and rematches show a short title card. The Four have their own looks, and each door adds a layer to their music.

Changed The Sandy Trail, the Clogged Dirt Road and the Dry Ice Corridor are redrawn, bigger and with more to see. Tall props turn see-through when you stand behind them. Fixed Every map was checked: people, signs and pickups no longer stand on walls or hide behind trees, and fences run the right way. If a map change left your save inside something, you are moved to the nearest open spot.

New The Aliens of Vicchio quest: help Mantequilla el Mexicano, who is picking mushrooms in the Bamboo Thicket, find three Glowing Caps while Peaking. It opens the Vicchio Crop Circle, home of a new Astral, the Vicchiomorph, and earns you his Sombrero. Fixed "Choose who goes next" in battle no longer covers your Serotonin panel.

Changed Day and night change more slowly and gradually: an in-game hour is about a minute of walking, with smooth dusk and dawn and a moon or sun sweeping across the screen when the day turns. Fixed House walls now look right from the sides.
Changed The first tap during the intro turns the sound on instead of skipping it. Opening the game after an update now starts the new version straight away.
New A GIOLEPPESOFT logo and an old-school animated intro when the game opens. Any button skips it.

New Quick Items: Q, I or the ITEMS button opens a panel to give snacks and water to any Astral without the Fanny Pack. Beaten wild Astrals sometimes leave a bottle or a snack behind. Banyan explains the four levels of high after you pick your starter, and a tip repeats it the first time you get high. Changed Key words in dialogue and battle messages are coloured: key items, items, Astrals, places and the rules of the game. Fixed Notices that came up at the same moment no longer overwrite each other.
New Options › Picture size: Full, Large, Medium or Small, always sharp. Fixed A question's choice box no longer flashes up before the question. Swaying trees no longer show stripes.
Fixed On phones, the music now starts on the first tap.
New Shift battle style: after knocking out a trainer's Astral you can swap yours for free before their next one comes out. Choose Shift or Set in Options.

Changed Audio levels evened out: the quiet Chai Tent tracks are louder, and sound effects are louder against the music. Tracks that shared the same melody in different keys now have melodies of their own.
Fixed On a phone in landscape, the on-screen controls no longer cover the text box. The MENU button on phones is bigger.

Changed You get high more slowly just from battling, so Peaking is a choice rather than something that creeps up on you. Ganjapod's line learns Side Eye at level 11 and Noodle Arm at 26, to help against Svetlana and Chloe. The Sunset Cliff's trainers and wild Astrals are a little lower in level.

New A push puzzle on a Sunset Cliff ledge, with a Neon Glowstick behind it. Changed The Flea Market, Sweetwater Lake and the Arabian Sea Shallows are reshaped (alleys, an island, sandbars), and five more maps get new details and hiding places.

New Two new legendaries, Sunraga and Bassilisk, each at the end of a quest. The Watcher in the Cave quest for Mandalord, with hints in the cave and in Banyan's diary. Changed Mandalord now gets a second chance: if it gets away, it is back the next time you enter the Sadhu Cave.

New The first release: the beach and the whole festival, eight bosses and their Wristbands, 36 Astrals to bag, Team Undercover, the Mainstage Temple with the Four and the VIP Shaman Council, an ending and an open festival afterwards. Plays in the browser on phones and PCs, with touch, keyboard and gamepad controls and key remapping. Installable as an app that works offline, with saves you can export and import.
