Screenshots taken from the game (version 1.2.5). Mild spoilers for places and bosses further into the story.

Chakra-geddon plays like an old handheld: a d-pad, an A button to confirm and a B button to go back. It works with a keyboard, a touch screen or a gamepad, and you can switch between them whenever you like.

Action Keyboard Touch screen Gamepad Move Arrow keys or W A S D D-pad D-pad or left stick Confirm, talk, read, open Z, Enter or Space A, or tap the picture A (bottom button) Back, cancel X, Esc or Backspace B B (right button) Run Hold X / Esc / Backspace while moving Hold B while moving Hold B while moving Open the Fanny Pack (menu) M or Tab MENU Start (or Select / Back) Quick Items Q or I ITEMS X (left button) Lick the blotter L LICK Y (top button)

Move with the d-pad. Walk into people and signs, then press A to talk to them or read them. On a touch screen you can also just tap the picture. Run by holding B while you move. You cover ground twice as fast. You cannot run while floating on water. Doors and exits are walked through. Walking off the edge of a map takes you to the next area. Stand still for a few seconds and your hero starts dancing. Stand still for much longer, outdoors, and they start licking the blotter out of boredom. Banyan did warn you. See Intoxication.

A moves dialogue on. If text is still typing out, A shows the rest of it. When a question comes up, pick an answer with the d-pad and confirm with A. A question ignores your button for a split second after it opens, so a hasty double press does not pick something by accident. Words in colour are special: key items in magenta, other items in amber, Astrals in teal, places in purple and game rules in blue.

MENU opens the Fanny Pack, your main menu (see The Fanny Pack). MENU or B closes it again. Up and down move through a list, A picks, B goes back a step. Left and right switch pages or change a setting where it makes sense. Everything can be tapped or clicked. Tap a row to pick it. Very small rows take two taps: the first moves the cursor there, the second confirms.

ITEMS (Q on a keyboard, X on a gamepad) opens a small panel without leaving the map: your snacks and water on the left, your party with their health bars on the right. Pick an item, then the Astral to give it to. Every item that heals or rehydrates turns up there by itself, and so does the blotter.

Pick commands and moves with the d-pad and A; B steps back. Hold B to fast-forward the play-by-play. Important lines (a boss's words, a change in how high you are) still wait for you to press A, so you never skip them by accident. MENU during a battle shows the log of everything that just happened, laid over the fight.

Keyboard keys can be changed in Options › Remap keyboard. Choose an action, then press the key you want for it. The arrow keys, Enter and Esc always keep working, whatever you change, so you can never lock yourself out. Reset to defaults puts everything back. Touch controls and gamepad buttons cannot be remapped.

Held upright, the picture sits at the top and a full set of controls sits below it. Held sideways, see-through controls sit in the margins. They lift out of the way when they would cover the text box. The LICK button appears once the blotter is in your fanny pack. Picture size in Options makes the picture smaller if you want more room round it.

Chakra-geddon runs in your web browser, on a phone or a computer. There is nothing to download and no account to make. Once it has loaded, it keeps working offline, so it is happy on a beach with no signal.

Go to gioleppe.github.io/chakrageddon in any up-to-date browser. Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari all work. The very first time, a notice called Before you go in explains what you are getting into: it is a satire about a festival, full of jokes about drugs and the people who take them, meant for adults, and fiction rather than advice. It also warns that some scenes wobble and flash. You choose: Play with effects: the full experience. Play in grounded mode (steady picture): keeps the screen calm. You can change this any time in Options. Then a short animated intro plays (it plays every time you open the game). Your first button press or tap turns the sound on; the next one skips the intro.

The game is a web app you can pin to your home screen. It then opens full-screen like any other app, and plays offline. iPhone or iPad (Safari): tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen. Android (Chrome): open the browser menu (⋮), then Add to Home screen or Install app. When a new version comes out, it downloads quietly in the background and takes over the next time you launch the game. tip On a phone held upright, the picture sits at the top and the controls below it. Turn it sideways and the controls float in the margins either side of the picture. Both work; pick whichever your thumbs prefer.

Continue picks up your saved trip. It only appears once you have a save. New trip starts from the beginning. If you already have a save, the game asks you to press again before it overwrites it. Options opens the settings (see Options).

There is one save per device, kept in your browser. The game saves by itself every time you move to a new area and after every battle. You can also save by hand at any time: open the Fanny Pack (MENU), go to System and choose Save. Continue on the title screen loads it. To move your trip to another device, use Export save to file in Options on the old one, then Import save from file on the new one. caution Your save lives in the browser's storage. Clearing your browsing data, or playing in a private window, can wipe it. If your trip matters to you, export a copy now and then.

You are lying on warm sand outside Driftwood Shack, passed out, while a white-bearded face blocks the sun. In this half-dream he explains the festival: it is full of Astrals, creatures that are what a state of mind looks like when it gets loose. People keep them as friends and battle with them. Wear a wild one down and it can be stabilised in a baggie. Serotonin is their health, Hydration their stamina. Eight festival bosses hand out Wristbands of Enlightenment, and with all eight the VIP Shaman Council will see you. He asks your name (Moonbeam, Dave or Ziggy) and lets you ask him one question. Then you wake for real, at 4:00 PM, face down on Driftwood Shack Beach. Your backpack, shoes and passport are gone. In their place: a fanny pack, half a bottle of warm coconut water, and a suspiciously glowing blotter. The old man is Prof. Banyan, who came to Goa in 1994 "for two weeks". Walk over to the shack and talk to him. He tells you your passport is with the Council at the Mainstage Temple, and offers you one Astral from his stash.

All three start at level 5. Banyan lets you look at each one and change your mind before you commit. Starter Type In Banyan's words What to expect Ganjapod Organic "A sleepy coconut. Slow, sturdy, and it heals itself on the couch." Tough and patient. Its Couch Lock traps the foe and heals Ganjapod every turn. The hardest start, on purpose: Organic is weak to two of the common early types. Jawling Stimulant "A gecko that never stops talking. Fast and fragile." Hits first and hits often. Its Unsolicited Life Story strikes two to five times and can tip the foe into a Thought Loop. Blottertot Psychedelic "A paper frog. Strange powers, and it bends the rules." A tricky one. Its Kaleidoscope Spit (learned at level 7) flips the whole type chart for a few turns. There is no wrong answer, only a different trip. The two you did not pick can still turn up later, if you know how to look (being very high helps). After you choose, Banyan hands you 5 Ziploc Baggies and 3 Coconut Waters, explains the four levels of high (see Intoxication), and takes down the festival tape that blocks the beach path. The first wristband is with DJ Diabolo at the Poi Pit, north along the Sandy Trail. note A ranger at the top of the Sandy Trail will not let you through to the Poi Pit while you carry only one Astral. Bag a second one in the incense clouds on the way. Talk to her and she gives you three baggies to help.

Open Options from the title screen, or during play from the Fanny Pack: MENU › System › Options. Change a setting with A, or with left and right. A short explanation of the setting under the cursor is shown at the bottom of the screen. Options are remembered on your device, separately from your save. They are not part of your trip, so you can change any of them at any time without consequences.

Setting Choices What it does Difficulty Easy / Normal / Hard How hard everyone hits. See below. Grounded mode On / off Caps the trippy screen effects at their mildest level, however high you are. Recommended if you are sensitive to motion or flashing. Reduced motion On / off Stops screen shake, flashes and spinning backgrounds. Scene changes become plain fades, and long animations become still pictures. Text speed Slow / Normal / Fast How fast dialogue types out. Battle speed Normal / Fast / Very fast How fast battles play out. Holding B also fast-forwards. Battle style Shift / Set What happens when you knock out a trainer's Astral. See below. Picture size Full / Large / Medium / Small Shrinks the picture in sharp whole steps, centred on black. The help line tells you the current size in pixels. Volume 0% to 100% Music and sound together, in steps of 10%. 0% is mute. Sound test Listen to the music of every area, the battles, the bosses and the title. Remap keyboard Choose your own keys. See Controls. Export save to file Downloads your save as a file, to keep as a backup or move to another device. Import save from file Loads a save file. This replaces the save on this device. Then choose Continue on the title screen. Defaults are in bold.

Difficulty changes only one thing: the damage moves do. Your Astrals' moves The other side's moves Easy hit 20% harder hit 20% softer Normal as they are as they are Hard hit 20% softer hit 20% harder Everything else stays the same: catching, prices, levels, water costs, how high you get. Damage from status conditions is not affected either. You can switch difficulty in the middle of your trip, even right before a boss you are stuck on. Nobody will know.

Shift (the default): when you knock out one of a trainer's Astrals, you are told which Astral they will send next and asked Swap Astral or Keep going. Swapping is free: your new Astral comes in before theirs does, and nobody takes a hit. Set: the trainer sends their next Astral straight in, and you fight on with whoever is out. Shift makes trainer fights noticeably friendlier. Set is for people who like it tense.

Being high in Chakra-geddon changes the picture: ripples, colour shifts, wobbling scanlines and, at the very top, ghost images and inverted colours on critical hits. It is a big part of the joke, but it is not for everyone. Grounded mode keeps the picture at the gentle level you would see at a light Come-up, however high your character gets. You lose none of the gameplay: the rules of being high still apply, only the screen stays calm. Reduced motion stops the movement: no shake, no flashes, no spinning title rays, no rainbow trails. It works on its own or together with grounded mode. The boss cutscenes and the intro never flash, whatever you choose. tip You can turn both on and off whenever you are free to open the Fanny Pack (MENU › System › Options). If a particular area or trip is too much, switch them on, get through it, and switch them back.

An Astral is what a state of mind looks like when it gets loose: a sunburned tourist who believes he is a crab, a balloon full of laughing gas, the guy with the bongos next to your tent at 7:30 AM. There are 41 of them at the festival. Some live in the incense, some only come out at night, during a particular set, or when you are high enough to see them. A few are one of a kind.

Every Astral has one or two types, and so does every move. Type What it feels like Psychedelic Visuals, third-eye entities, sacred geometry. Stimulant Hyper-speed, techno-gremlins, endless chatter. Dissociative Gravity-bending, noodle limbs, horse spirits. Organic Earthy, munchie beasts, chill golems. Downer Couch-lock sloths, warm blanket ghosts. Bummer Shadow people, siren noises, existential dread. There is also a seventh kind of move, Normal, which has no type at all: it hits everyone the same, and never gets the same-type bonus. No Astral is Normal. Types are always written out as words in the game, never shown by colour alone.

Read across from the move's type to the defending Astral's type. Move ↓ / Defender → Psychedelic Stimulant Dissociative Organic Downer Bummer Psychedelic 1 1 2 2 ½ ½ Stimulant 1 1 ½ 2 2 ½ Dissociative ½ 2 1 ½ 1 2 Organic 1 ½ 2 1 2 ½ Downer 2 ½ 1 ½ 1 2 Bummer 2 1 ½ 2 ½ 1 2 means "It really resonates!" (double damage). ½ means "It barely registers..." (half damage). Everything else is normal damage. A few things worth knowing: Two types multiply. A move that is doubled against both of a defender's types hits four times as hard. One doubled and one halved cancel out. Same-type bonus. A move that matches one of the attacker's own types hits 1.5 times as hard. No type resists itself. A Psychedelic move hits a Psychedelic Astral normally. The chart can flip. A few moves, and one boss, turn the chart upside down for a few turns: double becomes half and half becomes double. When everything feels backwards, it is. In battle, once you have seen an Astral before, the move panel tells you whether a move resonates or is weak against it. On an Astral's summary, point at a type and press A for a reminder of what it beats and what beats it.

Each Astral has six stats, shown on its summary page: Stat What it does Serotonin Its health. Vibe Attack How hard its physical moves hit. Ego Defense How well it takes physical moves. Fractal power How hard its astral moves hit. Groundedness How well it takes astral moves. BPM Its speed. The faster Astral moves first. Hydration, the water for its moves, is a separate pool (see Battles). Moves are physical (Vibe Attack against Ego Defense), astral (Fractal power against Groundedness) or status (no damage, something else happens).

Every Astral has one ability, the same for its whole evolution line. It works by itself. Ability What it does Second Wind Once a battle, it heals a quarter of its Serotonin when it drops below a third. Overdrive Below a third of its Serotonin, moves of its own type hit 30% harder. Clear Head Cannot fall into a Thought Loop or a K-hole. Thick Skin Takes 20% less from physical moves. Dreamer Drifts out of the way of one attack in seven. Stamina Every move costs one less Hydration. Static Cling A physical hit on it can leave the attacker with Cottonmouth. Grounded Critical hits never land on it. Sharp Eyes Lands critical hits more often. Burst Its first move after coming out hits twice as hard. Then it pops. Mirror Copies the first move used on it, for the rest of the battle. The last two belong to one Astral each. You will know them when you meet them.
Astrals level up ("peak") by earning Vibes in battle, up to level 60. With each level they grow a little stronger, and now and then learn a new move.

Stats do not grow by a fixed amount. Every level-up rolls the dice: Hydration grows by nothing (40% of the time), 1 (50%) or 2 (10%). The other stats grow around their species' usual rate, sometimes a point more, sometimes a point less. So two Astrals of the same kind at the same level are never quite the same. Each one keeps its own luck for life, through evolution too. Each evolution line also has a growth schedule for each stat: some stats grow early, some late, some steadily. Everyone grows steadily up to level 10. Between 10 and 24 the early bloomers pull ahead, and after that the late ones catch up. Point at a stat on the summary page and press A: the note tells you how that Astral grows it. tip A late bloomer that looks a bit weedy at level 18 may well be the best Astral in your party at 35. Give it time.

Many Astrals change into a stronger form. Most do it by reaching a level, right after a battle they won or an Astral was bagged in. A few can also be pushed along with a catalyst item, used on them from the Stash Tin. Astral Becomes How Ganjapod Hashlump, then Charagolem Level 16, then level 36 Jawling Gurnagama, then Amphetadragon Level 16, then level 36 Blottertot Fractoad, then Hoffmanite Level 16, then level 36 Crabcake Lobsterlad Level 22, or a Warm Kingfisher Ketacrab Wonkrab Level 24 Snoozel Duvetghast Level 20, or a Banana Lassi Mozzquito Dengoth Level 27 Djembe-Monk Bongo Bishop Level 25 Shroomba Omeletron Level 26 Tridog Omnihound Level 28 Shadowcop Bribe-asaurus Level 30 Wooklet Grand Wook Level 30 Glowkid Ravelord Level 32, or a Mystery Powder The starters' final forms pick up a second type: Charagolem is Organic and Downer, Amphetadragon Stimulant and Bummer, Hoffmanite Psychedelic and Dissociative. A catalyst does nothing to an Astral that does not use it. Mystery Powder also gets you a little higher. Nobody will say what is in it.

Your Trip Journal (in the Fanny Pack) keeps track. An Astral you have only seen gets a blue ballpoint sketch; one you have bagged gets its full picture and notes. Press A on any Astral you have seen and its Where page lists every place it lives, at what levels, and when: by day or night, during a set, on land or water, or only once you are high enough. See Bagging Astrals.
You do not catch Astrals here. You bag them: wear a wild one down in battle, then "stabilise" it in a bag. That is how you make friends at this festival.

Find a wild Astral and fight it. Wear it down. The less Serotonin it has left, the better your chances. Choose BAG and pick a bagging item. Watch it shake. Three shakes and it is yours: "Bagged!" If it breaks free, the turn goes on as usual and you can try again. "So close! It wriggles free." means it was a near thing. You can only bag wild Astrals. Trainers do not take kindly to it.

Item Price How good Ziploc Baggie Rs 60 The basic one. Works best on a worn-out Astral. Rizla Paper Rs 180 Wraps tighter: 1.6 times the baggie's chance. Amber Vial Rs 420 Lab-grade containment: 2.4 times the baggie's chance.

Low Serotonin. An Astral on its last sliver of health is about three times as easy to bag as a fresh one. A status condition. An Astral with any status (Cottonmouth, a K-hole, Ego Death, Jaw Lock) is half as easy again to bag. A better bag. See above. Being high. From the Come-up your bags hold better, and Peaking or beyond better still (up to 1.3 times). But see the catch below. The Astral itself. Common Astrals are easy; rare ones fight the bag; legendary ones are very hard indeed. To give you a feel for it: a common crab at full health in a plain Ziploc Baggie goes in about one time in four. Worn down to almost nothing, about three times in four. Worn down and with a status, it is practically guaranteed.

The higher you are, the clumsier your hands. When you are Peaking, one bag in ten simply flutters off into the night before it touches anything ("Your hands are not your hands."). At Ego gone it is three in ten. The bag is used up either way. What counts is how high you were when the battle started. See Intoxication.

You carry up to six Astrals. When your party is full, a newly bagged Astral goes to the stash, which Chai Mama keeps at every Chai Tent. You can swap Astrals between your party and the stash whenever you sit at a tent (see Chai Tents and Whiteouts). Give your new friend a nickname from its page in the Fanny Pack, if you like: pick a suggestion, or type one of up to 12 characters.

High-only Astrals only show themselves to people who are Peaking or beyond. Somebody in each place where one hides will drop a hint, and the Journal and the map mark it with a little eye. Night Astrals only come out after dark. Set Astrals only come out while a particular set is playing (see The Festival Timetable). One-of-a-kind Astrals wait at the end of quests. If you run from one, or knock it out by accident, it usually comes back for another try later. Bring your best bags.

The Journal tab in the Fanny Pack is a duct-taped notebook with a page for every Astral. An Astral you have never met is a row of question marks. One you have seen gets a blue ballpoint sketch and its types. One you have bagged gets its full picture and Banyan-style field notes. The counter at the bottom shows how many you have seen and bagged. An eye next to an unseen Astral means something only visible when high lives somewhere you have already been. The page tells you where: "Get higher to see it." Press A on any Astral you have seen to open its page. Switch between Where and Notes with left and right (or a tap), and scroll with up and down. Where lists every place it lives, with levels and conditions: by day or at night, during a set, from a certain level of high, on land or on water. It also covers gifts and one-of-a-kind Astrals, and what it evolves from and into. Notes has the full journal entry, once you have bagged one.

Banyan loves a full Journal. Drop in on him on Driftwood Shack Beach now and then, and he rewards you as your collection grows: Astrals bagged Banyan gives you 10 5 Rizla Papers 20 3 Amber Vials 30 3 Masala Chai All 41 Rs 5000 and 2 Mystery Powders, and a speech

Nobody at this festival fights with fists any more. Too much effort. Conflicts are settled on the astral plane, one Astral against one Astral, taking turns. Battles start in two ways: Wild Astrals drift out of encounter tiles: clouds of Nag Champa incense, dark bush, packed dancefloors, and water once you can float on it. A wild fight comes every few steps on those tiles, never right on top of the last one. Trainers watch in a straight line. Walk into their line of sight and they shout "!", walk up to you, say their piece, and fight. You cannot run from a trainer: "There is no walking away from eye contact." You carry up to six Astrals. The first one standing in your party goes out first.

Every Astral has two bars. Serotonin is its health. Hits drain it. At zero the Astral fades out and cannot fight again until it is revived or rested. Hydration is water for its moves. Every move costs water, shown as "Water" next to the move. Strong moves are thirsty. When an Astral cannot afford any of its moves, it can only Dry Heave: a weak, free hit that hurts itself too. Keeping your team watered matters as much as keeping it healthy. Water Bottles and Electrolyte Sachets refill Hydration, and a Chai Tent fills everything. See Items and Shops.

Command What it does FIGHT Use one of your Astral's moves (up to four). BAG Throw a bagging item at a wild Astral, or use a recovery item on one of your party. ASTRALS Switch to another Astral. That uses up your turn. RUN Try to get away. Wild battles only. Switching, bagging and running always happen before anybody's move that turn. Running does not always work, but every failed try makes the next one more likely, and it is easier if your Astral is at least as fast as the wild one.

The move panel shows, for the move under the cursor: its type, its power ("Pow"), or "Status" for a move that does not deal damage, its water cost, in red if your Astral cannot afford it, and, once you have seen the foe before, a hint: resonates (it will hit hard) or weak (it will barely register). For the full story of a move (accuracy, effects and odds, in plain words), look it up on the Astral's summary in the Fanny Pack.
Some moves always go first (Jawling's Unsolicited Life Story is one). Otherwise the Astral with the higher BPM (speed) moves first. A tie is a coin flip.

Moves can miss. The game says it "drifts wide". Moves that only affect the user never miss. A move that matches one of the user's own types hits 1.5 times as hard. Type matchups can double or halve the damage, or more (see Astrals and Types). "It really resonates!" means it was super effective; "It barely registers..." means it was not. Critical hits do 1.5 times the damage. They get more common the higher the battle is: from about one hit in sixteen when everyone is sober to one in four at the very top. That goes for both sides.

An Astral can have one status at a time. A Thought Loop is the exception: it can come on top of another status. The battle screen shows a short tag next to the Astral's name. Status Tag What it does Cottonmouth DRY Its physical moves hit half as hard, and it loses 3 Hydration at the end of every turn. K-hole K-HOLE For 2 to 4 turns its BPM drops to a quarter, and half the time it cannot move at all ("has forgotten what limbs are"). Thought Loop LOOP For 2 to 5 turns, about a third of the time it either repeats its last move or hits itself in confusion. Ego Death EGO It does nothing for 3 turns, then comes back with its Groundedness up 2 stages. Jaw Lock JAW It loses Serotonin at the end of every turn, a little more each time, until it is cured. How to get rid of them: Tiger Balm cures any status, Thought Loops included. An Electrolyte Sachet cures Cottonmouth. Switching out ends a Thought Loop. A status ends when the Astral fades out, and every status is cleared by a rest at a Chai Tent. Statuses stay after the battle until something cures them. Check your party. The Clear Head ability, and the Sand Mala held item, stop Thought Loops and K-holes from happening at all. Earplugs in your bag make your Thought Loops a turn shorter.

Some moves raise or lower stats for the rest of the fight: Vibe Attack, Ego Defense, Fractal power, Groundedness and BPM. "Rose!" is one stage, "rose sharply!" two. A stat can go up to six stages up or down. Each stage up adds half again, so two stages doubles a stat. Stat changes last until the Astral leaves the field. Switching out resets them, the good ones as well as the bad.
Each Astral can hold one item, which works by itself in every battle. Give one from the Astrals page or the Stash Tin in the Fanny Pack. The held items are listed in Items and Shops.

Beat an Astral and your team earns Vibes (experience). The Vibes are shared between the Astrals that were sent out against it and are still standing. Trainers' Astrals give twice as many as wild ones, and the higher you are, the more you earn (see Intoxication). With enough Vibes an Astral peaks: it goes up a level, its stats grow a little (by luck, see Astrals and Types), and now and then it learns a new move. An Astral knows up to four moves. When it wants to learn a fifth, a page shows the new move's numbers and, under the cursor, what each move does. Pick the move to forget, or Skip the new one. The game asks once more before you give a move up. Nothing is lost for good: Juniper the tarot reader can bring forgotten or skipped moves back later (see Juniper's Tarot). Beaten wild Astrals sometimes leave something behind: usually water or coconut water, sometimes a melon slice or a sachet, rarely Tiger Balm. Trainers pay you in rupees instead.

A trainer brings one to six Astrals and sends the next one in when one fades out. You cannot bag a trainer's Astral ("You cannot bag somebody else's trip.") and you cannot run. Under the Shift battle style (the default), when you knock out one of their Astrals you are told who comes next and may Swap Astral for free before it arrives, or Keep going. See Options. Wraparound Shades in your bag make trainers notice you from one tile less far away. When your own Astral fades out, you must choose who goes next.

The eight wristband bosses, and a few other big names, get the full treatment: An entrance. The music drops, the crowd turns and the camera slides over to them. A cutscene introducing them, with their own title card. Their own stage. Each boss fights on a set of their own, to their own theme music. The moment. The first time a boss's team falls to half its total Serotonin, the boss says one line and changes the fight: the music speeds up and their Astral gets faster, the type chart flips, everyone gets higher, they heal, or their team toughens up. Be ready for it. The ceremony. Win, and the crowd cheers while you receive your wristband and learn what it lets you do (see Wristbands and Techniques). Lose, and you white out (see Chai Tents and Whiteouts). When you come back for another go, the cutscene plays again in full. The tent and shops next to a boss's stage stay shut until that boss is beaten. Come prepared.

Every wristband boss eventually offers a stronger rematch, about ten levels up, with the same moment at half health. It becomes available once you have collected a couple more wristbands after beating them. DJ Diabolo only takes his during his headline set at the Poi Pit, and he will tell you when to come back. The Promoter's waits until after the credits. Rumour has it that beating all eight rematches wakes something under the Mainstage.

When your last Astral fades out, you do not black out. You white out. You lose some rupees and possibly an outfit, and wake up hours later at the last tent where you rested. The details are in Chai Tents and Whiteouts. At the very top of your high, you may meet your own reflection: a battle against a copy of your own party. Losing to it costs nothing at all. Winning gives nothing either. It is a reflection.

The striped Chai Tents are your safe havens. Inside each one, Chai Mama (a tired woman in a crochet top who has seen everything, twice) looks after anyone who staggers in. Walk up to a tent and press A. She asks: Rest, Check the stash or Leave.

"Here is watermelon and a heavy blanket." A rest: restores all Serotonin and all Hydration for your whole party, and for every Astral in the stash; cures every status condition, and revives fainted Astrals; brings you all the way down to a Microdose; makes this tent your whiteout point: where you wake up if you lose; adds this tent to your tuk-tuk stops, once you can ride (see Travel). It costs nothing. "Do not tell me what you saw." Once you have the Festival Timetable, Chai Mama also offers to let you sleep until a set starts. Pick which set from the timetable, soonest first, and the night goes by on a clock in the dark. If the set is right there at that tent, you get a look at the crowd and the stage as you wake. See The Festival Timetable.

You carry up to six Astrals. Everyone else waits in the stash, which Chai Mama keeps at every tent. When your party is full, newly bagged Astrals go straight there. Choose Check the stash and your party page opens with the stash unlocked. From there you can: Take an Astral from the stash into your party (if you have room); Swap with... a party Astral, in one go; Send to stash one of your party (you must keep at least one); read anyone's Summary. Sort the stash by order caught, name or level with the chip at the top (or left and right). Away from a tent you can still look at who is in the stash, but not swap. "Swap at a Chai Tent: Chai Mama keeps the stash." Checking the stash also makes the tent your whiteout point.

The Sunrise Guesthouse at the Flea Market has a bed for Rs 100 a nap. Banyan's hammock, in his shack on Driftwood Shack Beach, is free. "It smells of incense and 1994." Both work like a Chai Tent's rest, without the stash.

Some Chai Tents sit right next to a boss's stage, and Chai Mama there will not patch you up for another go at them: "Not while DJ Diabolo is still on, beta. Everyone who walks in mid-set wants a blanket and a second go." Until that boss is beaten, the tent: does not heal, is not a whiteout point, and is not a tuk-tuk stop. The shops in those areas keep their shutters down too. So heal up before you walk onto a boss's turf, and bring snacks. The Mainstage Temple's tent is a special case. It works until you start your climb against the Four-on-the-Floor. Once you have beaten one of them, Chai Mama will not let you sit until you have beaten all four: "You started. Finish, then sit."

Chai Tent Notes Driftwood Shack Beach Your first. Open from the start. The Poi Pit Opens once DJ Diabolo is beaten. The Tantric Yurt Opens once Guru Svetlana is beaten. The Sunken Scooter Ditch Opens once Captain Keta is beaten. The 5 AM Omelette Stall Opens once Chef Raju is beaten. 190 BPM Forest Stage Opens once Baron Von Darkpsy is beaten. The Sunset Cliff Opens once Influencer Chloe is beaten. The Last Dancefloor In the welfare tent, on the way to the temple. Mainstage Temple At the foot of the temple. Shut during the climb.

When your last Astral fades out, you do not black out. You white out: "You have nobody left standing. Everything goes white..." Then: You lose some rupees. 15% of what you carry, or more if you were high: 22.5% when Peaking, 30% at Ego gone. One random outfit you own walks off with somebody. (If you own none, you lose none.) Six hours pass. You wake at your last resting place, with your whole party and stash fully healed, stone sober. "Somebody has tucked you in." You keep your Astrals, their levels and Vibes, your items (apart from that outfit), your wristbands and your quest progress. Lost an outfit? A shop outfit is back in stock, so you can buy it again. For a gift outfit, go back to whoever gave it to you: they always seem to have a spare.

The boss stays where they are, at full strength, and you can try again whenever you like. Their cutscene plays again in full. The nearby tent is still shut, so your whiteout point is wherever you rested before. Losing halfway up the Mainstage Temple sends the Four back to their posts: the climb starts over from the bottom.

At Ego gone you may end up fighting your own reflection. Losing to it is not a whiteout. "Your reflection wins. It does not seem to mind." Everything is put back the way it was. tip A whiteout costs a share of the rupees you carry, so the more you carry, the more you lose. Before a risky fight, spend your rupees on things you will use anyway (bags, water, a Weighted Blanket), and come down before a boss if you can: it halves the bill compared with Ego gone.
It is an infinite seven-day festival, so something is always playing somewhere. Once you know the timetable, you can be in the right place at the right time.

After your third wristband, the next time you arrive somewhere, Prof. Banyan jogs up beside you with his photocopy of the Festival Timetable, folded into eighths. It adds a Sets tab to the Fanny Pack and pink markers on the map. Before that, the stages are just stages: no sets play.

The Sets tab shows the festival clock and every set in order of start time. The set playing now is marked LIVE. A set starting within two hours says how long until it begins ("in 40m", "in 1h"). The set under the cursor shows where it plays, until when, and what it is like. On the region map, a pink marker shows where a set is on right now.

Time Set Where What happens 06:00 to 08:00 Sunrise set Driftwood Shack Beach A slow, beautiful set as the sun comes up over the water. Banyan never misses it. Neighbula comes out. 08:00 to 10:00 Ecstatic dance The Tantric Yurt Svetlana's morning session: gongs, bare feet and a lot of breathing. A gong player, and Chillem. 17:00 to 20:00 Night market Anjuna Flea Market The market stays open into the dark. A night vendor sells things nobody sells by day, and Bribe-asaurus turns up. 18:00 to 20:00 Sponsored sunset The Sunset Cliff Chloe livestreams the sunset. Everybody faces the sea, and the phones. A camera girl, and Sirenowl. 21:00 to 03:00 Generator Disco The Load-In Road The crew's own party in the truck park. A DJ, festoon lights, lasers, and a dancing Glowkid. Only once the power is back. 22:00 to 01:00 Diabolo headline set The Poi Pit The Pit is packed and the strobes go wild. An MC, Ravelord, and the only time Diabolo takes on a rematch. 02:00 to 05:00 Darkpsy hour 190 BPM Forest Stage Fog, UV and 200 BPM. A UV painter, and Nitroxide. 05:00 to 07:00 The 5 AM rush The 5 AM Omelette Stall Every wrecked raver on the island queues for an omelette. A raver in the queue, and Omeletron.

The Generator Disco is not on the timetable at first. The Load-In Road's three generators have all died at once, and somebody read a memo about cutting the power. Get all three running again (the quest Power Cut) and the crew throw their own party every night from 21:00. It then appears on the Sets page like any other set.

The area fills with a crowd. On the big dancefloors every tile is packed. The music switches to the set's own mood and tempo, and "Live now" appears as you arrive. Someone special turns up for the occasion. A set-only Astral comes out of the encounter tiles. These Astrals appear nowhere else in the wild, and they come out during their set whether it is day or night. Some quests and some people also care about which set is on. The Journal's Where page lists a set-only Astral's set once you have seen it.

You do not have to walk the clock round. Once you have the timetable, Chai Mama offers you more after a rest: Rest at any Chai Tent. When she asks "...Sleep here until a set starts?", choose Sleep until a set. Pick the set you want from the list, soonest first. A set at this very tent is marked "here". The night goes by on a clock in the dark, and you wake as the set begins. If it is right where you are sleeping, the camera goes over to the crowd and the stage before Chai Mama speaks. tip Combine this with the tuk-tuk: rest at the tent nearest the set you want, sleep until it starts, and walk straight into the crowd. For the Darkpsy hour, rest at the Forest Stage's tent; for Diabolo's headline set, the Poi Pit's.

"Out here everything gets you a little high: every fight, every snack, the air." — Prof. Banyan How high you are is the game's big dial of risk and reward. Higher means more Vibes, better catches and rarer Astrals. It also means harder wild fights, clumsy hands and costlier whiteouts. How high to fly is your call.

There are four levels of high. Once you are past a Microdose, the band shows in the corner of the screen, and the Fanny Pack always shows a meter with your band under it. Microdose Come-up Peaking Ego gone Vibes from battles normal +20% +40% +60% Bagging odds normal +15% +30% +30% Bags that fumble none none 1 in 10 3 in 10 Wild encounters normal 8% more often 16% more often 25% more often Rare, high-loving Astrals a little more likely more likely most likely Wild Astral levels normal normal +1 +2 Rupees lost on a whiteout 15% 15% 22.5% 30% Astrals that only show when high yes yes, and more Critical hits also get more common the higher a battle is, for both sides. A fight also has its own level of high: it starts at yours, nudged up by the Astrals in it (some of them are trippier than others), and moves with certain moves and boss moments. For Vibes, bagging and fumbles, what counts is the band you were in when the battle started. When you enter a new band, a line tells you so: "You are coming up. Wild Astrals feel closer, and every fight teaches a little more." "You are peaking. Rare Astrals come out to look at you. So do the strong ones. Your hands are getting unreliable." "Ego gone. Everything is an Astral and every Astral is enormous. Drink some water, or do not."

The Glowing Blotter. It is in your fanny pack from the very start, and it never runs out, "which is the problem". Each lick takes you up about one band: three licks from stone sober takes you all the way to Ego gone. Lick it with L, the LICK button on a phone, Y on a gamepad, from Quick Items, or from the Stash Tin. Not in the middle of a battle. Boredom. Stand still outdoors for about 25 seconds with the blotter in your bag, and your hand finds it by itself. "Everybody does. Keep moving." Boredom never takes you past Ego gone, and nobody licks a blotter out of boredom in somebody's living room. Battles. Every fight leaves you a little higher than before, more so after a trippy one. Mystery Powder, some moves, and a couple of bosses' moments.

Walking. Every step brings you down a tiny bit. A long walk sobers you up slowly. A Water Bottle. Giving one to an Astral means you take a sip too: about one band down. It always works, even when the Astral is not thirsty. A rest. Chai, watermelon and a heavy blanket at any Chai Tent (or a bed) brings you all the way down to a Microdose. A whiteout also leaves you stone sober, among other things.

The rules above are only half of it. The festival itself looks different. From the Come-up: the picture starts to ripple and the colours get richer. Glowing things get a soft halo, and the music picks up a warm pad underneath. Encounter tiles shimmer where a high-only Astral is waiting. Peaking: the screen sways in waves to the beat, and mandalas fade in on the ground near you. About fifty people at the festival suddenly have something different to say. Some people only show up when you are Peaking, and some quests only move forward in this state. Ego gone: the world wobbles and doubles, rainbows trail behind you, and text starts to scramble. You will see things that are not there (or are they?). Some places only exist while your ego is gone, and the moment you come down they fold shut and put you somewhere else. On the beach and the trail you might run into your own reflection, who wants a battle with your own team.

Some Astrals simply do not exist for sober people. A few appear from Peaking, the rarest only at Ego gone, and some of those only at night or on the water. Each place where one hides has somebody who drops a hint until you have seen it. The map and the Journal mark those places with a little eye.

In the game, yes, mostly. Nothing is permanent: rest at a tent and you are back to a Microdose. The real risks are practical: wild Astrals come more often and hit harder, you waste bags on fumbles, and a whiteout costs you up to twice as much money. A good rhythm for many players: get high to train and hunt rare Astrals near a tent, then rest before a boss. tip If the wobbling screen is too much, turn on Grounded mode in Options. The rules of being high still apply, but the picture stays calm.
documents.s: Is it safe to be high?

documents.t: Everything you carry lives in your Stash Tin (the bag page of the Fanny Pack). You start with Rs 300, a warm coconut water and a glowing blotter. Rupees come from beating trainers, finishing quests, and selling things you do not need.

From the Stash Tin: pick an item. Healing items and catalysts ask which Astral to use them on; held items ask who should hold them; clothes go on (or come off); key items tell you what they are. From Quick Items: press ITEMS (Q on a keyboard) on the map for a quick panel of snacks and drinks next to your party's health bars. See Controls. In battle: choose BAG. Only bagging and recovery items can be used there. The first row of the Stash Tin sorts it: By type, A to Z or Most first.

Item Price Effect Ziploc Baggie Rs 60 Stabilises a wild Astral. Works best when it is worn out. Rizla Paper Rs 180 Wraps tighter than a baggie. Better odds. Amber Vial Rs 420 Lab-grade containment. Rarely fails. More in Bagging Astrals.

Item Price Effect Coconut Water Rs 40 Restores 25 Serotonin. Watermelon Slice Rs 120 Restores 60 Serotonin. Masala Chai Rs 300 Restores all Serotonin. Water Bottle Rs 50 Restores 40 Hydration. You take a sip too, which brings you down about one band. Electrolyte Sachet Rs 150 Restores all Hydration and cures Cottonmouth. Tiger Balm Rs 90 Cures any status condition, Thought Loops included. "Smells like a decision." Weighted Blanket Rs 600 Brings a fainted Astral back with half its Serotonin. A Water Bottle works on an Astral that is already full of water, for the sake of your sip. Nothing else heals a fainted Astral except a Weighted Blanket or a rest at a Chai Tent.

Gear is used from the Stash Tin, or simply works while you carry it. Item Price Effect Incense Stick Rs 150 Light it from the Stash Tin: keeps wild Astrals away for 120 steps. Wraparound Shades Rs 800 While you carry them, trainers notice you from one tile less far away. Earplugs Rs 400 While you carry them, your Astrals shake off Thought Loops a turn sooner.

A catalyst makes certain Astrals evolve on the spot. Use it from the Stash Tin on the Astral you want to change. It does nothing to the others. Item Price Evolves Warm Kingfisher Rs 700 Crabcake into Lobsterlad Banana Lassi Rs 700 Snoozel into Duvetghast Mystery Powder Rs 900 Glowkid into Ravelord. Also gets you a little higher. Nobody will say what is in it.

Give one to an Astral from its page on the Astrals tab (Hold item), or pick it in the Stash Tin and choose who holds it. Each Astral holds one item, and it works by itself in every battle. Take it back returns it to your tin. Item Price Effect Friendship Band Rs 700 Heals a sixteenth of its Serotonin at the end of every turn. Neon Glowstick Rs 900 Its moves hit 10% harder. Lucky Rupee Rs 600 A coin with a hole in it. More critical hits. Steel Flask Rs 650 Its moves cost a third less Hydration. Sand Mala — Its holder keeps a clear head: no Thought Loops, no K-holes. A quest reward. Several held items can also be earned by helping people around the festival.

Outfits are purely cosmetic: they change how your hero looks on the map and in their portrait. Put them on and take them off from the Stash Tin. Your bandana, shades and wristbands always stay on (hats hide the first two). Outfit Price Where Tie-Dye Shirt Rs 400 Beach Stall. "Pink, swirly, faintly damp." Cotton Kurta Rs 500 Beach Stall. Sequin Vest Rs 800 Flea Market, Merch Stall. "Catches every laser in the valley." Glow Jacket Rs 900 Flea Market, Night Market, Merch Stall. Festival Poncho — A thank-you from somebody at the Sunrise Guesthouse. Crab Suit — A lilo and two oven gloves, from the Crab Raver. Sombrero — If anyone asks, you are from Vicchio. Clothes are one of a kind. While you own an outfit, the shop shows it as "Sold out". Sell it back and it is in stock again. The same goes for held items. caution A whiteout costs you one random outfit. It walks off with somebody while you are out. A shop outfit comes back into stock, so you can simply buy it again. For a gift outfit, go back to whoever gave it to you: they always seem to have a spare.

Key items are for the story and for quests. They never run out, cannot be sold, and choosing one in the Stash Tin reads it to you. They include: Glowing Blotter: lick a corner to go up a band. It never runs out. See Intoxication. Festival Timetable: Banyan's photocopy, folded into eighths. It opens the Sets page (see The Festival Timetable). Passport: yours, slightly chewed. Eventually. Memos, crates, coconuts, coloured sands, a bent antenna and other quest things. People will tell you what they are for.

Talk to a stallholder to open their shop. Buy shows the stock, Sell shows what you can sell, Leave closes it. Each press of A buys or sells one. Selling pays half the price. Key items, and things that were free, cannot be sold. Shop Where Sells Beach Stall Driftwood Shack Beach; another stall at the Poi Pit Ziploc Baggies, Coconut Water, Water Bottles, Tiger Balm, Tie-Dye Shirt, Cotton Kurta Anjuna Flea Market The market's main stall Baggies, Rizla Papers, Coconut Water, Watermelon, Water Bottles, Electrolyte Sachets, Tiger Balm, Incense, Wraparound Shades, Earplugs, Warm Kingfisher, Banana Lassi, all four held items, Sequin Vest, Glow Jacket Night Market The Flea Market's night vendor, during the Night market set (17:00 to 20:00) Amber Vials, Mystery Powder, Warm Kingfisher, Banana Lassi, Neon Glowstick, Electrolyte Sachets, Glow Jacket Toddy Shack Fishermen's Cove Coconut Water, Watermelon, Water Bottles, Electrolyte Sachets Crew Catering The Load-In Road Masala Chai, Banana Lassi, Watermelon, Coconut Water, Water Bottles Backstage Bar The Backstage Container Amber Vials, Rizla Papers, Masala Chai, Watermelon, Electrolyte Sachets, Tiger Balm, Weighted Blankets, Mystery Powder Merch Stall The Last Dancefloor Amber Vials, Rizla Papers, Weighted Blankets, Electrolyte Sachets, Glow Jacket, Sequin Vest Shops in a boss's own area keep their shutters down until that boss is beaten: "House rule: nothing sold mid-set." That includes the Poi Pit stall and the Backstage Bar.

Pickups lie around the festival. Walk up to one and press A. Some only show under a blacklight, some only at low tide, and some only when you are high. Wild Astrals you beat sometimes leave a drink or a snack behind. Prof. Banyan rewards a growing Trip Journal (see Bagging Astrals). Quests pay in rupees, items and the occasional outfit. The Quests page in the Fanny Pack keeps track.

"I read past lives. Only for Astrals, though. People's past lives are all Cleopatra. It got boring." Juniper is a tarot reader in round glasses and a mustard beanie, and her table smells of oat milk and palo santo. For a fee, she helps an Astral remember a move it has forgotten, skipped, or never got round to learning.

After your sixth wristband, the next time you arrive somewhere, Prof. Banyan drops in. Or rather, his astral body does: a see-through, violet-glowing Banyan who floats down out of the sky. ("My body is at home in the hammock. This is only my astral body. Very convenient. Terrible for the back.") He tells you a card reader has set up at the Anjuna Flea Market. Her table is there from then on. The first time you sit down, she riffles an enormous deck by candlelight and turns over a card.

A reading costs Rs 500: one Astral, one move remembered. "Cards don't lie, but they don't do refunds either." Talk to Juniper and choose A reading. Pick an Astral. Your party is laid out as tarot cards, each with how many moves it could remember. One with none has "its past all here already". Pick a move from its past. Every move is shown with a note on what it does. If the Astral already knows four moves, pick the one it forgets to make room. Confirm. The cursor starts on "No", so you cannot pay by accident. Choose How does it work? for Juniper's own explanation, or Not now to leave. ("Mercury is in retrograde anyway.")

An Astral can remember any move that: its evolution line learns at or below its current level, including moves that only its earlier forms learn, and it does not already know. So a move learned at level 30 is not on offer to a level 25 Astral, but a move you skipped at level 12 is. A Charagolem can remember things it learned back when it was a Ganjapod.

You skipped a move when your Astral learned something new, and now miss it. Evolution moved on and an old favourite from the first form is gone. You need coverage: a move of another type, or a heal, or a status move, for a particular boss. Water troubles: a cheaper move can keep an Astral fighting longer than a thirsty strong one. tip Before you pay, look at the Astral's moves on its summary page in the Fanny Pack (point at a move and press A). Then decide which one is worth Rs 500 to bring back, and which one can go.

Your backpack is gone. What you have instead is a fanny pack, and it holds everything: your Astrals, your stuff, your notes and your sense of direction. Press MENU (M or Tab on a keyboard, Start on a gamepad) to open it, and MENU or B to close it. The tabs run down the left side. Pick one with up and down and A, or tap it. Under the tabs you always see your rupees and a meter of how high you are. Tab What it is Astrals Your party, their summaries, held items, nicknames, and the stash. Stash Tin Your bag: items, clothes, the blotter, gear. Journal The Trip Journal: every Astral you have seen and bagged. Map The region map, your current goal, a hint, and the tuk-tuk. Sets The festival timetable. Appears once Banyan has brought it. Quests Side quests, active and finished. Wristbands Your eight Wristbands of Enlightenment, in fake 3D. Log The last 80 lines of dialogue, battle messages and notices. System Save, Options and Unstuck.

Your party, in order: the one at the top goes out first in battle. Each row shows the Astral's level, its Serotonin and Hydration bars, and a tag if it has fainted (OUT) or has a status. Pick an Astral for: Summary: its full page (see below). Move: change the party order. Pick an Astral, then the slot to swap it with. Send to stash: only while you sit at a Chai Tent. Hold item: give it a held item from your tin, or Take it back. Nickname: pick one of the suggestions or type your own, up to 12 characters. Choose its own name to go back to it. Below the party is the stash, sorted by order caught, name or level (tap the chip, or press left and right). Pick a stashed Astral to Take it, Swap with... a party Astral, or read its Summary. Taking and swapping only work at a Chai Tent.

The summary shows an Astral's types, Serotonin, Hydration, how many Vibes until it next peaks (levels up), its stats, its four moves, its ability and its held item. Point at anything on it (with the d-pad, or a tap) and press A, and it explains itself in plain words: a move: its power, accuracy, water cost and every effect, with the odds; a stat: what it does, and whether this Astral grows it early, late or steadily; a type: what it hits hard and what hits it hard; the ability and the held item. This is the best place to learn the game's rules as you go.

Your bag, in a brushed-metal tin. The top row sorts it By type, A to Z or Most first. The item under the cursor shows its category and description below the list. Pick an item to use it: healing items and catalysts ask which Astral; held items ask who should hold them; clothes go on or come off (the one you wear is marked "worn"); key items tell you about themselves; the blotter gets licked. Bagging tools wait for a wild Astral. See Items and Shops.

The Trip Journal, a duct-taped notebook with a coffee ring on it. It lists all 41 Astrals: question marks for those you have not met, a ballpoint sketch for those you have seen, and the real picture and notes for those you have bagged. Press A on a seen Astral for its Where page (every place it lives, and when) and its Notes. Details in Bagging Astrals.

The top of the page shows your current goal ("Beat DJ Diabolo in the Poi Pit for the Hemp String Wristband.") and a hint on which way to go next ("Next: head north to the Poi Pit."). The same hint appears under the area's name whenever you arrive somewhere new. On the drawn map: Red squares are hubs; yellow squares are other places; grey ones you have not visited yet, shown as "???". Your head bobs on the place you are in. A red flag marks your goal. A small tent marks every place where you have rested at a Chai Tent. A yellow "!" means somebody there has a quest for you. A pink marker means a set is playing there right now. An eye means a high-only Astral still hides there. Move the cursor between places with the d-pad, or tap one. Once you have the VIP Press Pass, place the cursor on a place with a tent you rested at and press A to ride a tuk-tuk there. See Travel.

Appears once Prof. Banyan has brought you the Festival Timetable. It shows the festival clock and every set, in order of start time: the one playing now is marked LIVE, and sets starting soon say how long until they begin. The set under the cursor shows where it plays, until when, and what it is like. See The Festival Timetable.

Your side quests. Active ones are listed with their next step; finished ones are greyed out underneath. Quest givers in the world show a "!" above their head, and people waiting for you to hand something in show a "?". "New quest" and "Quest complete" are announced as they happen.

Your eight Wristbands of Enlightenment. The list is on the left; the one selected turns slowly in fake 3D beside it, each made of its own material. Under it: who gave it to you, a description, and what it lets you do. A band you have not earned yet is a dark silhouette with a question mark. See Wristbands and Techniques.
The last 80 lines of dialogue, battle messages and notices, in case something scrolled past too fast. "Nothing has happened yet. Give it time."

Save writes your progress to this device. The game also saves by itself whenever you change area and after battles. Options opens the settings (see Options). Unstuck: walled in, or lost? This takes you back to where you came into the current area. Nothing else changes. The game asks first, with "No, stay here" on the cursor. Anything you pushed around in the area rolls back too. tip Unstuck is there for the rare moment you trap yourself, say behind a subwoofer you shoved the wrong way. It never costs you anything, so use it freely.
A satire. Hydrate. Look after each other. And also:

Talk to everybody. People hint at hidden Astrals, hand out quests, and occasionally give you things for free. A "!" over someone's head means they have a quest for you. Bag a second Astral early. The ranger at the top of the Sandy Trail will not let you through with just one, and a second Astral is a lifesaver against the first trainers anyway. Incense clouds are where the wild ones drift out. Read the summary. In the Fanny Pack, open an Astral's summary, point at a move and press A. It tells you exactly what the move does. Same for stats, types and abilities. Use Quick Items. Q, ITEMS or X on a gamepad heals your party from the map without digging through menus.

Every move costs Hydration. Strong moves cost a lot. An Astral that runs dry can only Dry Heave, and that hurts it too. Carry Water Bottles. They are cheap (Rs 50), they refill 40 Hydration, and the sip you take brings you down a band. Electrolyte Sachets refill an Astral completely. Mix cheap and strong moves. A cheap move that does the job is often better than a big one that leaves you parched three fights later. Trainers do not drink in battle. You can. That is a real advantage in a long fight.

Play the type chart. Doubled damage is a big deal, and a matching type adds another 1.5 times on top. The move panel says "resonates" once you have seen the foe before. Switch out of a bad matchup. Switching costs a turn, but it also clears a Thought Loop and any lowered stats. Use the free swap. With the Shift battle style (the default), when a trainer's Astral goes down you can swap yours in before the next one appears, without taking a hit. Share the Vibes. Every Astral sent out against a foe, and still standing at the end, gets a share. Start a fight with a weaker Astral and switch to your strong one to train both. Watch for the boss moment. At half their team's health, every boss changes the fight. Keep something in reserve. Struggling with a boss? Gain a couple of levels, buy some Watermelon Slices and Water Bottles, or try Easy difficulty for that fight. Options are not part of your save, so nobody will know.

Get high to train. More Vibes, better bags and rarer Astrals make the Come-up and Peaking great for levelling and collecting. Come down for bosses. Wild Astrals hit harder when you are high, your bags fumble, and a whiteout at Ego gone costs twice as much money. A Water Bottle or a rest fixes it. Keep moving. Standing around outdoors with the blotter in your bag leads to licking it out of boredom. Ego gone has secrets. Some Astrals, some places and some moments only exist at the very top. Have a look around, at least once, near a tent.

Rest at every tent you pass. It heals everything, sobers you up, sets your whiteout point and adds a tuk-tuk stop for later. Heal before a boss's area. The tent next to a boss's stage stays shut until that boss is beaten, and so do the shops there. Spend before risky fights. A whiteout takes a share of the rupees you carry.

Wear them down, give them a status, then bag. Low health and a status condition together make most Astrals easy. Peaking helps, Ego gone hurts. Your bags hold better from the Come-up, but at Peaking one in ten fumbles, and at Ego gone three in ten. Check the Journal's Where page. It tells you exactly where, when and how high you need to be to find an Astral you have seen. Visit Banyan. He rewards a growing Journal at 10, 20, 30 and all 41. Look at the map for eyes. An eye marks a place where an Astral only visible when high still hides.

Bump into obstacles. If something blocks your path, walking into it tells you which wristband and which type of Astral you need. Keep a mix of types. Field techniques need a party member of the right type. Without a Dissociative Astral you will not float, and without a Psychedelic one the dark stays dark. Follow the hint. The Map tab always shows your next goal and which way to head. Unstuck is free. Trapped yourself behind a subwoofer? Fanny Pack, System, Unstuck.

The game saves by itself whenever you change area and after battles, and you can save from the System tab any time. There is one save per browser. Export it now and then from Options, especially before clearing your browser data or switching devices.

The festival stretches along the coast from Anjuna to Arambol: beaches, stages, jungle shortcuts, a flea market, a sacred cow in the middle of the road, and eventually a temple. Most of it you cover on foot, which is fine, because nobody here is going anywhere in particular anyway.

Walk with the d-pad. Walk off the edge of a map, or through a door, to reach the next area. Run by holding B. You move twice as fast. "Everyone at this festival is in a hurry. Nobody knows where to." You cannot run while floating. Encounter tiles (incense clouds, dark bush, packed dancefloors, water if you are floating) bring wild Astrals. Light an Incense Stick to keep them away for 120 steps. Trainers watch in a straight line. Step into it and the fight is on. Sometimes you can sneak round; often you cannot. Some ways are shut until you have the right wristband and the right Astral with you (see Wristbands and Techniques), or until somebody lets you through. Bump into what blocks you and it tells you why. Lost? The Map tab in the Fanny Pack shows your goal and the way to go next. Stuck in a corner? System › Unstuck puts you back where you came into the area.

The festival never stops, but the clock does move. It is shown on the Sets page once you have the timetable. A new trip starts at 4:00 PM. The clock only moves when you walk. One festival minute passes every seven steps, so an hour goes by in a bit over a minute of walking. Standing still, talking, shopping and fighting take no time at all. Sleeping at a Chai Tent until a set, waiting for the tide, and whiting out (six hours) all move the clock forward.

It is night from 7 PM to 6 AM. The light fades slowly over a couple of hours at dusk and dawn, and when the day turns a band of sky sweeps across the top of the screen: a moon and "Night falls", or a sun and "The sun comes up". At night: the Flea Market, the Omelette Stall, the Poi Pit, the Sandy Trail and the Tantric Yurt have different wild Astrals; some Astrals and some people only come out after dark; battles get a night backdrop. Several things happen only at certain hours: the sets on the Festival Timetable, the tides at Fishermen's Cove, a sunrise errand, a sunset legend. People will mention them.

Beat Influencer Chloe and her VIP Press Pass gets you the Share Taxi Tuk-Tuk. "Tuk-tuk drivers salute it." Open the Fanny Pack and go to the Map tab. Move the cursor to a place with a tent marker: somewhere you have rested at a Chai Tent. The label says A: tuk-tuk. Press A. A yellow and green tuk-tuk bounces you down the night road, horn first, and drops you at that tent. Every Chai Tent you rest at becomes a stop. So rest at every tent you pass. A few places are out of a tuk-tuk's reach: you cannot call one from deep inside the temple, a sea cave or a room that exists only in your head. Walk out first.

At the east end of Driftwood Shack Beach, a lifeguard turns you back from the rocks until you have four wristbands. Beyond them lies Fishermen's Cove: a fishing village with boats pulled up on the sand, nets drying, a toddy shack with its own shop, and the sea with two islets. From the cove, a cliff path leads to the Sunset Cliff. Coming down it is free; going up needs the Banyan Root Climb.

The flats between the shore and the islets are only dry at low tide. The painted tide table on the sign says it all: Low tide High tide 4 AM to 10 AM 10 AM to 4 PM 4 PM to 10 PM 10 PM to 4 AM At low tide the flats are wet sand you can walk across. Some things out there can only be reached then. At high tide the surf covers them and nobody can cross. "The sea does not care about your plans." If the tide turns while you are out on the flats, you splash back to the nearest dry sand. Flat rocks let you sit and wait for the tide to go out. "It thinks about it for a long time, and then it goes."

Rosa in the village has a problem with her grandfather's boat (see the quest Low Tide). Help her, and from then on Rosa rows you up the coast to the Arabian Sea Shallows and back, whenever you like. Talk to her on either beach. "It is quicker than walking, and the dolphins are free."

Beyond the velvet rope behind the Backstage Container lies the festival's last and biggest dancefloor, the road to the Mainstage Temple. It is packed. Dancing lanes: on many rows the crowd dances sideways, one tile with every step you take, in groups with gaps between them. Some rows move faster, some slower, some the other way. Nobody dances onto you, and walking into a dancer simply makes you wait a beat for a gap. You can never be boxed in. Watch the rhythm and step through. Superfans of every boss wait along the way, and wild Astrals live in the thickest crowds. The welfare tent near the start has a Chai Tent and a merch stall. At the very front, the crowd might just give you a lift. They are picky about who they lift.

To get your passport back from the VIP Shaman Council, you need all eight Wristbands of Enlightenment. Each one is handed over by a stage boss after you beat them, and each one (bar the last) unlocks a field technique: a way past something that blocked your path. So the bosses are also the keys to the map.

Techniques never take up a move slot, and you never have to select them. One fires by itself when you walk into, or face, the obstacle it clears, as long as: you own the wristband, and somebody in your party has one of the types it needs. Without those, walking into the obstacle tells you what you would need. So when something blocks your path, bump into it and read. Technique Needs a party member of type What it does Machete Hack Organic or Stimulant Hacks through tangled fairy lights and bamboo. Cleared for good. Blacklight UV Pulse Psychedelic Lights up dark places, which are otherwise only lit right around you. It also reveals hidden pickups. Bass Drop Shove Downer or Organic Shoves subwoofers and passed-out wooks one tile. They roll back when you leave the area. Pink Flamingo Float Dissociative Lets you float across foam pits and shallow water. Jaw Grind Stimulant Chews through padlocked VIP fences. Share Taxi Tuk-Tuk any Rides a tuk-tuk to any Chai Tent you have rested at, from the Map tab. See Travel. Banyan Root Climb Organic or Psychedelic Climbs the banyan roots that hang down the cliffs. tip Keep a mix of types in your party. A team without a Dissociative Astral cannot float, however many wristbands you have. If a technique will not fire, check your party's types, or swap someone in at a Chai Tent.

Floating: while afloat you cannot run, and in some places wild Astrals live in the water too. Shoving: some subwoofers have to be pushed in the right order, and some ledges jam if you push straight in. If you box yourself in, Unstuck (Fanny Pack, System) puts you back at the area's entrance and rolls everything back. Dark places: before you have the Blacklight UV Pulse, you can still walk them, but you only see a little circle around you. The last band opens the velvet rope behind the Backstage Container, and the road to the temple beyond it.

The Wristbands tab in the Fanny Pack shows your collection. The eight bands are listed on the left, each with a dot of its colour. The one you select turns slowly in fake 3D, seen a little from above, each in its own material: three twisted strands of hemp, rose quartz beads, a split ring with a rubber duck and a bottle opener swinging off it, a greasy cheese-yellow stamp band, black rubber with glowing bones, a lanyard with a laminated pass, a smudge of holy ash, and a hologram whose colours run as it turns. Under it: who gave it to you, a description, and what it lets you do. A band you have not earned is a dark silhouette with a question mark, and tells you whose it will be: "Beat Captain Keta for this one." With Reduced motion on, the bands stand still.

Wristbands also open up other parts of the festival: After the third, Prof. Banyan brings you the Festival Timetable (see The Festival Timetable). After the fourth, the lifeguard at the east end of the beach lets you round the rocks to Fishermen's Cove (see Travel). After the sixth, a tarot reader sets up at the Flea Market (see Juniper's Tarot). Every boss offers a rematch a while after you beat them (see Battles).

Spoilers This page explains how to find every secret Astral in the game. Six Astrals never turn up in an ordinary patch of incense. Three are true legendaries, and three more only show themselves to people who are very, very high. On top of those, a few Astrals come to you as gifts or one-off encounters. # Astral Type Level Where Needs 36 Mandalord Psychedelic / Organic 37 Sadhu Cave, east wall The Unfinished Mandala, sober 37 Sunraga Psychedelic / Stimulant 42 Sunset Cliff Team Undercover exposed, 5 to 8 PM, Peaking 38 Bassilisk Downer / Bummer 50 Backstage Container All eight rematches won, after the credits 39 Vicchiomorph Dissociative / Psychedelic 28 Vicchio Crop Circle The Aliens of Vicchio; night; Peaking 40 Mirrorling Dissociative 27–30 Arabian Sea Shallows, water Ego gone 41 Lucidra Psychedelic / Downer 27–30 Sweetwater Lake, water Ego gone, at night Legendaries are hard to bag: their catch rates are the lowest in the game (Mandalord, Sunraga and Bassilisk 15, Vicchiomorph 20, Mirrorling and Lucidra 35; a Crabcake is 190). Bring a stack of Amber Vials, wear them down to a sliver of health, and give them a status condition if you can, which makes every bag 50% more likely to hold. Being Peaking or Ego gone also helps the odds (by 30%), but makes your hands shake: a bag can flutter off into the night before it even lands (10% of throws while Peaking, 30% with your ego gone). The good news: none of the three legendaries can be lost. If one gets away or you knock it out, it comes back.

Psychedelic / Organic · Clear Head · Lv 37 A sand mandala on the Sadhu Cave's east wall that nobody ever finished. Beat Baba Smoke and he asks you, in smoke, to finish it: four coloured sands, each from a different corner of the map. Shell Sand (white): Driftwood Beach, on the tide line, at sunrise (5 to 7 AM). Kumkum (red): Pujari Mohan at the Roadside Shrine, once Lakshmi is off the road. Turmeric (yellow): beat Line Cook Anil behind the Omelette Stall. UV Powder (glow): a jar at the Forest Stage that only shows while you are Peaking. Lay them on the wall sober (Microdose), and the pattern turns and Mandalord steps out. If it slips away, leave the cave and come back. Once it is in your Journal, Baba sweeps the mandala away and gives you a Sand Mala. The step-by-step is in The Unfinished Mandala. Its ability, Clear Head, means it can never fall into a Thought Loop or a K-hole. Lead Lakshmi of the Four has one of her own, at Lv 41.

Psychedelic / Stimulant · Overdrive · Lv 42 The sunset itself. Nobody can see it come out while Team Undercover's fence is up on the Sunset Cliff. Expose Team Undercover: bring the three memos to the hippie in the Flea Market (Team Undercover's Plan). The quest The Freed Sunset starts. Be on the Sunset Cliff between 5 and 8 PM while Peaking. If you arrive early, the Sunset Watcher in the south-west will sit with you until 6 PM. The sun stops halfway into the sea, turns round and looks at you from the cliff's edge, in front of the crowd. Reach out to it. If it drops into the sea instead of into your bag, it will be back at the next sunset ("for the ones who are high enough to see it"). Sunraga is weak only to Bummer moves. Its signature move is Golden Hour.

Downer / Bummer · Grounded · Lv 50 The bass under the Mainstage, and the strongest wild Astral in the game. Finish the game. The Last Drop starts after the credits. Win all eight boss rematches (rematch list). The Promoter's own rematch only opens after the credits. Go to the Backstage Container. The speaker stack in the north-east corner is humming a note too low to hear. Reach into the bass. If it sinks back into the speakers, walk out and back in. Bassilisk takes almost nothing from Psychedelic moves (a quarter) and resists Bummer. Hit it with Dissociative or Downer moves. Its Grounded ability means it never takes a critical hit, so luck will not save you. Its signature move is Sub Drop.

Dissociative / Psychedelic · Dreamer · Lv 28 A lanky grey-green visitor on a pocket-sized saucer, with stars in its very big, very black eyes. Do The Aliens of Vicchio for Mantequilla in the Dense Bamboo Thicket: three Glowing Caps found while Peaking, then a landing at night. A path opens east through the bamboo to the Vicchio Crop Circle. The saucer only hovers over the circle at night (7 PM to 6 AM), and only for people who are Peaking. Wave back. If it zips up into the stars, leave the crop circle and come back. Its ability, Dreamer, makes it drift out of the way of one attack in seven. Its signature move is Close Encounter. Psychedelic, Organic and Downer moves hit it hard.

Dissociative · Mirror · Lv 27–30 A wild Astral that only exists for people whose ego has gone. Float out on the water of the Arabian Sea Shallows while Ego gone (lick the blotter well past Peaking) and it can turn up among the crabs and Neighbula. Its ability, Mirror, copies the first move used on it into its own moveset for the rest of the battle. Open with something you would not mind being hit by. Psychedelic and Organic moves hit it hard.

Psychedelic / Downer · Dreamer · Lv 27–30 Like Mirrorling, but stranger. Float out on Arambol Sweetwater Lake while Ego gone, and at night: it only surfaces after 7 PM and before 6 AM. Stimulant, Organic and Downer moves hit it hard. tip Ego gone hits hard both ways: wild Astrals come out two levels higher, and a whiteout costs twice as many rupees. Spend your money before you go fishing for Mirrorling and Lucidra, and keep Water Bottles handy to come down a band.
These are not legendary, but you only get them one way, or only once.

Ganjapod, Jawling and Blottertot, Lv 5, from Professor Banyan at the start: you pick one. The other two are wild, but only while you are Peaking: Ganjapod on Driftwood Beach (Lv 3–4), Jawling on the Sandy Trail (Lv 4–6) and Blottertot in the Poi Pit (Lv 6–8).

The reward for Peak Experience: a Nitroxide, Lv 25. Nitroxide is also wild in the Scooter Ditch, the Sea Shallows' water, the Dry Ice Corridor, the Sunset Cliff and the Load-In Road, and at the Forest Stage during Darkpsy hour. Its ability, Burst, makes its first move after coming out hit twice as hard; then it pops at the end of its second turn.

Once only, in the fog in the middle of the Dry Ice Corridor. Pay it Rs 500 and a sheepish Shadowcop, Lv 25, drifts out. Refuse and you face a Bribe-asaurus, Lv 29. Either is a wild battle, so you can bag it.
