Omelette Stall Chef Raju (the Back Alley is 19–22) 20–23 23–24 6. Forest Stage Baron Von Darkpsy 22–25 26–27 7. Sunset Cliff Influencer Chloe 25–26 27–28 8. Sadhu Cave Baba Smoke 31–33 33–34 9. Backstage The Promoter 35–37 37–38 10. Last Dancefloor The Front Row 39–40 40–41 11. Mainstage Temple Astra-Zero, the last time 39–43 42–44 12. After the credits The Promoter's rematch, then Bassilisk 45–47, then 50 48–50 tip Getting high makes everything faster: Peaking gives 40% more Vibes per fight and Ego gone 60% more. It also makes wild Astrals stronger and your bagging hands clumsier, so try it on a route you already know. A night in a Chai Tent brings you all the way down.

The festival sprawls along the coast of North Goa. On the region map (the Map tab in your Fanny Pack) it looks like this: The south-west is where you start: Driftwood Shack Beach, with Banyan's shack. The Sandy Trail runs north from it to the Poi Pit, and the Tantric Yurt sits north of the Pit. The middle is the Anjuna Flea Market, the first hub, with the main shop and the Sunrise Guesthouse. Four roads leave it: west to the Yurt, north up the Clogged Dirt Road (with the Jungle Shortcut and the Roadside Shrine as detours round the cow), east through the Back Alley, and south into the Dry Ice Corridor. The north is water: the Sunken Scooter Ditch at the top of the Dirt Road, then the Arabian Sea Shallows with the Sea Grotto on its islet and the Sadhu Cave in the cliffs behind. Arambol Sweetwater Lake lies to the east. The east is jungle: the 190 BPM Forest Stage south of the lake, the Dense Bamboo Thicket (and the hidden Vicchio Crop Circle), and the 5 AM Omelette Stall, the second hub. The south is the business end: the Sunset Cliff below the Dry Ice Corridor, Fishermen's Cove between the cliff and the beach, the Load-In Road east of the cliff, the Backstage Container, the Last Dancefloor, and the Mainstage Temple in the far south-east corner.

Each wristband teaches a field technique. Techniques never take a move slot: they work by themselves when you walk into the obstacle, as long as you have the wristband and an Astral of the right type in your party. This is why the bosses are also the keys to the map. Wristband From Technique Needs in your party What it does Hemp String Wristband DJ Diabolo Machete Hack Organic or Stimulant Cuts through fairy lights and bamboo Quartz Wristband Guru Svetlana Blacklight UV Pulse Psychedelic Lights up dark places and shows hidden items Wonky Keychain Captain Keta Bass Drop Shove Downer or Organic Shoves subwoofers and passed-out wooks Extra Cheese Stamp Chef Raju Pink Flamingo Float Dissociative Floats you over foam pits and shallow water UV Skeleton Band Baron Von Darkpsy Jaw Grind Stimulant Chews through padlocked VIP fences VIP Press Pass Influencer Chloe Share Taxi Tuk-Tuk Anyone Rides to any Chai Tent you have rested at, from the Map Ash Mark Baba Smoke Banyan Root Climb Organic or Psychedelic Climbs banyan roots on cliffs All-Access Hologram The Promoter Gets you past the velvet rope to the Mainstage

Chai Mama's tents heal your whole party and your stash, sober you up, and become the place you wake up after a whiteout. There are tents on Driftwood Beach, in the Poi Pit, the Tantric Yurt, the Scooter Ditch, the Omelette Stall, the Forest Stage, on the Sunset Cliff, at the Last Dancefloor and at the foot of the Mainstage Temple. Banyan's hammock and the Sunrise Guesthouse bed (Rs 100) heal too. In a boss's zone the tent stays shut until you beat the boss ("Win first. Then sit, and I will pour."), and so does any shop there. Heal up before you walk in.
You have your passport back. The festival goes on, and so does the game: the goal line now just says "fill the Trip Journal". Here is what is left to do.

Every wristband boss offers one stronger rematch, with the same half-health moment. Talk to them again once you have enough wristbands. Most of these open up before the credits. Boss Available Their team DJ Diabolo 3 wristbands, only during his headline set (10 PM to 1 AM, Poi Pit) Djembe-Monk Lv 18, Wooklet Lv 18, Glowkid Lv 20 Guru Svetlana 4 wristbands Blottertot Lv 22, Tridog Lv 22, Fractoad Lv 24 Captain Keta 5 wristbands Ketacrab Lv 26, Wooklet Lv 26, Nitroxide Lv 25, Wonkrab Lv 28 Chef Raju 6 wristbands Shroomba Lv 29, Lassiblob Lv 29, Chillem Lv 30, Omeletron Lv 32 Baron Von Darkpsy 7 wristbands Sirenowl Lv 33, Dengoth Lv 34, Fractoad Lv 34, Omnihound Lv 37 Influencer Chloe 8 wristbands Selfiend Lv 37, Gurnagama Lv 37, Bongo Bishop Lv 38, Ravelord Lv 40 Baba Smoke 8 wristbands Omeletron Lv 41, Grand Wook Lv 41, Chillem Lv 41, Hoffmanite Lv 42, Charagolem Lv 43 The Promoter After the credits Bribe-asaurus Lv 45, Ravelord Lv 45, Duvetghast Lv 45, Wonkrab Lv 46, Omeletron Lv 46, Amphetadragon Lv 47 The strategies from each boss's chapter still apply: only the levels have changed. If you ask Diabolo outside his set, he tells you to come to the Pit at twenty-two hundred. "Do not be late, I start without anyone."

Winning all eight rematches wakes something under the speaker stacks Backstage. The Promoter's quest, The Last Drop, tracks it. Go to the Backstage Container and look at the humming speaker stack in the north-east: Bassilisk, Lv 50, the strongest wild Astral in the game. See Legendaries.

Mandalord, from The Unfinished Mandala, if you did not finish it before the temple. Sunraga, at sunset on the Sunset Cliff, once Team Undercover is exposed and only while you are Peaking. Vicchiomorph, after The Aliens of Vicchio. Mirrorling and Lucidra, in the water, only with your ego gone. All of them are on the Legendaries and one-of-a-kinds page.

There are 41 Astrals. Banyan rewards you each time you show him a new milestone on Driftwood Beach: Bagged Banyan gives you 10 5 Rizla Papers 20 3 Amber Vials 30 3 Masala Chai All 41 Rs 5000 and 2 Mystery Powder "Every single one. The whole state of mind of this festival, in one duct-taped notebook. I think I can finally go home. I will not, but I could." The ones people miss: Your two other starters and their middle forms only appear while you are Peaking: Ganjapod on the beach, Jawling on the Sandy Trail, Blottertot in the Poi Pit, Fractoad in the Tantric Yurt, Hashlump at Sweetwater Lake and Gurnagama at the Forest Stage. Their final forms: Hoffmanite (Sadhu Cave, Ego gone), and Charagolem and Amphetadragon on the Last Dancefloor. Sets: no Astral is set-only, but sets are the earliest way to meet some of them: Bribe-asaurus at the Night market, Ravelord at Diabolo's headline set and Omeletron at the 5 AM rush, all at Lv 20–24, long before they turn up in the wild. See the timetable in chapter 5. Night-only: Shadowcop and Mozzquito show up on the early routes only at night (they are wild by day further on). Evolutions: Lobsterlad, Duvetghast and Ravelord can also come from a catalyst (Warm Kingfisher, Banana Lassi, Mystery Powder) instead of a level. The full table, with every location and level range, is in the Astral Journal. On the Map tab, an eye marks any zone where a high-only Astral you have not seen yet is still hiding.

Anything you skipped is still waiting. The full list is on the Side quests page. The most rewarding ones to mop up after the credits: The Crab Rave: the Crab Suit and a crab dance. Peak Experience: a Nitroxide. Lost Crates: a Neon Glowstick, or Rs 1500 if you keep one. Power Cut: Earplugs and the Generator Disco.

With nothing left to lose but rupees, this is a good time to see what Ego gone does to the world. Your reflection may challenge you on the beach or the trail, a memory vendor who looks like you sets up in the Flea Market, the cow walks off into the jungle, Banyan's diary has a page you have never seen, and stairs of light lead out over the sea from the Sunset Cliff.
Goal: beat Baba Smoke for the Ash Mark. Suggested level: 33–34. This is a big jump from Chloe, and Baba brings five Astrals.

With six wristbands, the next time you arrive somewhere, a see-through, violet-glowing Banyan floats down out of the sky. "Do not panic. My body is at home in the hammock. This is only my astral body." He tells you a card reader has set up a table at the Anjuna Flea Market. Juniper (round glasses, mustard beanie) reads the past lives of Astrals. For Rs 500 an Astral remembers one move its line learns by its level that it does not know now: a move it forgot, skipped, or could have learned as an earlier form. Useful for getting a strong old move back before the big fights ahead.

Go back to the Arabian Sea Shallows (by the Scooter Ditch, the lake, or by tuk-tuk to the Scooter Ditch's tent and a short float). The sadhu at the cave mouth in the north now steps aside. Float across to the ledge under the cliffs and go in. If you finished Low Tide, Rosa can also row you from Fishermen's Cove up to the Shallows' beach.

"Silence. (Smoke permitted.)" A dark cave of tunnels, candles and smoke. Baba sits on his cushion at the far north end. There is no Chai Tent here: heal before you come, and bring plenty of Masala Chai. On the east wall is a faded pattern, a circle inside a square cut into four, with a few grains of colour still clinging to it. It does nothing yet. Remember it. Trainer Astrals Yogi Dhruv (west, looks around) Duvetghast, Chillem, Lassiblob, all Lv 29 Disciple Tara (east, looks around) Omeletron, Omnihound, Grand Wook, all Lv 30 Items: 2 Masala Chai in the north-east corner, and two hidden ones: a Mystery Powder on the west side and 2 Amber Vials in the south-east corner. Wild: Chillem, Omeletron, Duvetghast, Grand Wook, Omnihound and Sirenowl (Lv 29–32). With your ego gone, Hoffmanite (Lv 31–33) too.

Baba never says a word. The smoke over his head does the talking: a question mark, then a wristband. Astral Type Level Weak to Omeletron Organic / Psychedelic 31 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant Grand Wook Organic / Dissociative 31 Psychedelic (four times), Organic Chillem Organic / Downer 31 Stimulant (four times), Organic Hoffmanite Psychedelic / Dissociative 32 Psychedelic, Organic, Downer Charagolem Organic / Downer 33 Stimulant (four times), Organic His moment: "Breathe in. Deeper. Now you are the smoke." The battle gets a lot more intoxicated, so critical hits come more often for both sides. Strategy: Psychedelic and Stimulant moves between them cover everything. A Ravelord (Stimulant / Psychedelic, from a Glowkid and a Mystery Powder) is perfect: its Psychedelic moves hit Grand Wook four times as hard and Omeletron and Hoffmanite twice, and its Stimulant moves hit Chillem and Charagolem four times as hard. Organic moves hit four of his five twice as hard (all but Omeletron). A Bummer Astral handles Omeletron (four times), but Grand Wook and Hoffmanite's Dissociative moves and Chillem and Charagolem's Downer moves hit it hard. Dissociative and Downer moves are mostly wasted here. Five Astrals means a long fight. Bring Masala Chai and a Weighted Blanket or two. Reward: Rs 3800 and the Ash Mark: not a band at all, but holy ash pressed round your wrist. It does not wash off. You tried.

Banyan Root Climb: with an Organic or Psychedelic Astral in your party, you can climb banyan roots on cliffs. Three sets of roots matter: The Omelette Stall's south exit: straight down to the Backstage Container. The shortest way to the last boss. The Sunset Cliff's east exit: onto the Load-In Road, which also ends at the Backstage. Fishermen's Cove's north-east corner: up to the Sunset Cliff.

Right after the fight, Baba points a long finger at the east wall, and the smoke draws the story: three figures in orange robes kneeling round the pattern with funnels of coloured sand, until a gust blows them away. Then he points at the wall, at you, and holds up four fingers. This starts The Unfinished Mandala, the quest for the legendary Mandalord. You need four coloured sands from all over the map, and one of them only appears after the Lakshmi quest. Baba draws you a map of what is still missing every time you talk to him. It is best done now or after the credits; Mandalord is Lv 37.

With your ego gone, the pattern on the east wall holds itself open like a door. Step through into the Inner Room, where an old woman who taught Baba Smoke, back when he was "a skinny boy with a lot of questions and no shoes", sits on the floor. Pick up the Mystery Powder she leaves for you. When you come down, the room folds shut and you are standing in the cave again. Rematch Baba offers a rematch once you have all eight wristbands: Omeletron, Grand Wook and Chillem Lv 41, Hoffmanite Lv 42, Charagolem Lv 43.

Goal: beat Baron Von Darkpsy for the UV Skeleton Band. Suggested level: 26–27. This is the biggest stretch of the map so far, with two optional areas (the Sea Grotto and Fishermen's Cove) and three side quests. Keep a Dissociative Astral in your party for floating, and a Psychedelic one for the dark Forest Stage.
documents.s: 6. Baron Von Darkpsy, the 190 BPM Forest Stage

documents.t: Two routes, and both are worth walking: By sea: from the Scooter Ditch, float north onto the Arabian Sea Shallows, cross the bay to its east edge, go east to Arambol Sweetwater Lake, then south to the Forest Stage. Through the bamboo: from the Omelette Stall, hack north into the Dense Bamboo Thicket, float across its channel, and go north to the Forest Stage.

A wide bay, mostly water. A long sunbathing beach runs down the west side, with sandbars and a sandy spit in the east, a rocky islet in the middle with the Sea Grotto inside it, and the Sadhu Cave's mouth up in the north cliffs (a sadhu with a staff turns you away until Chloe is beaten). East is the lake, south the Scooter Ditch. On the beach, Sharon from Basildon and her party have used cooking oil as sun cream ("factor nothing") and are going red: Mad Dogs and Englishmen. caution Finishing Mad Dogs and Englishmen turns the four tourists blue and happy, and they stop fighting. If you want to battle Nigel, Tracy and Dave, do it before you bring Sharon the clay. Trainer Astrals Lobster Nigel Lobsterlad Lv 22, Ketacrab Lv 22 Tracy from Leeds Neighbula Lv 22, Lassiblob Lv 23 Dave, Shirt Off Wonkrab Lv 23, Mozzquito Lv 23 Lifeguard Rohan Nitroxide Lv 23, Sirenowl Lv 24 Items: 2 Water Bottles: under a towel at the south end of the beach. 2 Amber Vials: on the ledge below the Sadhu Cave's mouth, in the north. 2 Coconut Water: on a sandbar in the north-east of the bay. Watermelon Slice: on the spit in the south-east. 2 Amber Vials (hidden): on a little sandbar in the south of the bay, west of the islet. Wild: almost everything here lives in the water: Ketacrab (Lv 20–23), Neighbula (Lv 20–24), Nitroxide (Lv 20–23), Lobsterlad (Lv 22–24) and Wonkrab (Lv 24). With your ego gone, Mirrorling (Lv 27–30) swims here too (see Legendaries).

Float to the islet in the middle and go in through the gap on its south landing. Inside it is dark, with tide pools. Smuggler Vasco: Mozzquito Lv 23, Lobsterlad Lv 24. Cave Diver Meera: Neighbula Lv 23, Nitroxide Lv 24. Cool Blue Clay at the very back, in the north-east: the thing Sharon needs. "THE CLAY IS AT THE BACK", as somebody scratched on the sign. Amber Vial (hidden) in the south-west corner. Wild: Ketacrab (Lv 21–24), Lobsterlad (Lv 22–25), Neighbula (Lv 21–24), Sirenowl (Lv 22–24).

A lake with a small island, a jetty and woods round the edge. "Things swim in the lake that do not swim anywhere else." Trainer Astrals Hippie Rain Lassiblob Lv 23, Neighbula Lv 23 Yogi Padma Duvetghast Lv 23, Snoozel Lv 22, Wooklet Lv 23 Items: Banana Lassi: in the north-west corner. Record Crate: in the north-east corner. One of three for Lost Crates. 2 Electrolyte Sachets: on the island in the middle (float out to it). 3 Watermelon Slices: on the east shore, in the south. Wild on land: Lassiblob, Neighbula, Wooklet and Tridog (Lv 21–24), Duvetghast (Lv 22–24), and rarely Omnihound (Lv 27–28) and Grand Wook (Lv 29). While Peaking, Hashlump (Lv 23–25). Wild in the water: Neighbula and Lassiblob (Lv 22–24), Wonkrab (Lv 24–25). At night with your ego gone, Lucidra (Lv 27–30).

North of the Omelette Stall. Fairy lights block the way in from the south and again further on, and a channel of water cuts the thicket in two. Wook Moss: Wooklet Lv 21, Chillem Lv 22. Fire-Spinner Ash: Glowkid Lv 22, Djembe-Monk Lv 22, Tridog Lv 22. Mantequilla is crouched in a gap at the east edge, picking mushrooms and humming. He drove from Vicchio, in Tuscany, in a Fiat Panda, following the aliens. Talk to him: The Aliens of Vicchio. Items: a Record Crate on the west side, a Warm Kingfisher in the north-east, 2 Electrolyte Sachets in the south-west and 1 Electrolyte Sachet (hidden) in the south-east. Wild: Wooklet, Glowkid, Shroomba, Chillem and Mozzquito (Lv 20–23), and rarely Grand Wook (Lv 29). In the water: Ketacrab and Neighbula (Lv 20–23).

A clearing in the jungle with a dancefloor, UV light, fog and glowing mushrooms. The trees pulse to the beat. It is dark: you need the UV pulse to see more than a few tiles. A Chai Tent in the south-west, shut until the Baron is beaten. A wook (west) with the hint you want: "His Astrals are Bummer and Psychedelic. Downers put both to sleep. I would know. I am one." The DJ Booth, the door in the north-east hut: Selector Nandini (Sirenowl Lv 26, Glowkid Lv 26, Dengoth Lv 27), a pickup of 2 Electrolyte Sachets, and a roadie whose record crates were dumped around the jungle (Lost Crates). Trainer Astrals Darkpsy Disciple Zed Glowkid Lv 24, Mozzquito Lv 24, Sirenowl Lv 24 Guard Lobo Shadowcop Lv 24, Dengoth Lv 24 Items: a Record Crate on the east side, 2 Tiger Balm in the south-west, and two hidden ones up north: a Mystery Powder in the north-east corner and a Tiger Balm in the north-west. Wild: Sirenowl, Tridog, Mozzquito, Glowkid and Shadowcop (Lv 21–24), Omnihound and Dengoth (Lv 24–25). While Peaking, Gurnagama (Lv 24–26). During Darkpsy hour (2 to 5 AM): Nitroxide (Lv 20–24).

He conducts the fog from the stage, facing away from the crowd. Walk up and talk to him. Astral Type Level Weak to Sirenowl Bummer 22 Dissociative, Downer Dengoth Bummer / Stimulant 23 Dissociative (four times) Fractoad Psychedelic 24 Downer, Bummer Omnihound Psychedelic / Bummer 25 Downer (four times), Bummer His moment: "One-ninety was the warm-up. Welcome to two hundred." His Astral gets two stages faster. Strategy: Downer moves hit Sirenowl, Fractoad and Omnihound hard (Omnihound four times). Duvetghast, Snoozel, Lassiblob or Chillem. Dissociative moves flatten Dengoth and Sirenowl. Neighbula (Dissociative / Downer) does both jobs at once and takes almost nothing from his Bummer moves. If you caught one at the Ditch, the Shallows or the lake, this is its fight. Psychedelic, Stimulant and Organic moves are resisted by three of his four. Leave them on the bench. After his moment his Astral will usually move first. Keep your healing items for then. Reward: Rs 2600 and the UV Skeleton Band.

Jaw Grind: with a Stimulant Astral in your party, you can chew through padlocked VIP fences. The ones that matter are at the Flea Market's south exit, which leads to the Dry Ice Corridor and the Sunset Cliff. Rematch The Baron offers a rematch once you have seven wristbands: Sirenowl Lv 33, Dengoth and Fractoad Lv 34, Omnihound Lv 37.

With four wristbands, the lifeguard at the east end of Driftwood Beach lets you round the rocks. Fishermen's Cove is a big, quiet area between the beach and the Sunset Cliff, and a good place to level up at this point (trainers Lv 17–21). The west: the Scramble, rock pools and dune grass. The north: a cliff-foot path under the red rock. Banyan roots at the far north-east climb up to the Sunset Cliff, but you need the Ash Mark for them (chapter 8). Coming down from the cliff later is free. The middle: a fishing village. Boats pulled up on the sand, nets drying, Rosa's hut and her grandfather Santan in his hammock, a fish stall, a little sea shrine, and the toddy shack, whose seller has a shop (Coconut Water, Watermelon, Water Bottles, Electrolyte Sachets). The east: a palm grove. The south: the sea, with two islets.

The flats between the shore and the islets are wet sand from 4 to 10, morning and evening, and surf the rest of the time. If the tide turns while you are out there, you splash back to the nearest dry sand. A tide table is painted on a sign, and flat rocks (one by the sign on the shore, and one out by each islet) let you sit and wait for the tide to go out. Rosa tells you that something came out of the sea and dragged her grandfather's boat, the Maria da Graça, into the cave on the islet: Low Tide. The Sea Cave is only reachable across the flats at low tide.

Trainer Astrals Shell Collector Maya Crabcake Lv 18, Lobsterlad Lv 19 Tidepool Wook Sunny Chillem Lv 18, Wooklet Lv 18, Shroomba Lv 19 Cliff Yogi Ananda Snoozel Lv 19, Lassiblob Lv 19, Duvetghast Lv 20 Angler Joaquim Crabcake Lv 19, Sirenowl Lv 20 Captain Furtado Ketacrab Lv 19, Wonkrab Lv 20, Lobsterlad Lv 21 Toddy Tapper Xavier Hashlump Lv 19, Chillem Lv 20 Lifeguard Priya Sirenowl Lv 20, Lobsterlad Lv 20, Neighbula Lv 21 Beach Cricketer Arjun Djembe-Monk Lv 19, Bongo Bishop Lv 20

2 Water Bottles: in the Scramble in the west. Amber Vial: in a nook under the cliff in the north-west. 2 Coconut Water: in the palm grove in the east. Tiger Balm (hidden): among the rocks just west of the village. 2 Electrolyte Sachets: out on the sandbar, low tide only. 3 Rizla Papers: on the little western islet, low tide only.

Day: Crabcake (Lv 17–19), Lobsterlad (Lv 18–21), Wonkrab (Lv 18–20), Sirenowl (Lv 18–21), Chillem (Lv 18–20), Neighbula (Lv 19–21). Night: Sirenowl, Duvetghast, Neighbula and Lobsterlad (around Lv 18–21). Water: Lobsterlad (Lv 19–22) and Wonkrab (Lv 19–21).

Across the flats, in the islet's cliff. Inside: the Maria da Graça wedged between the rocks with something enormous snoring in her, a Mystery Powder on the east side, a Masala Chai in the west, and wild Wonkrab and Lobsterlad (Lv 21–24), Sirenowl and Duvetghast (Lv 21–23), and Lobsterlad in the water.
Goal: beat Captain Keta for the Wonky Keychain. Suggested level: 18–19.
documents.s: 4. Captain Keta, the Sunken Scooter Ditch

documents.t: From the Flea Market, go north past the security guard onto the Clogged Dirt Road. Keep a Psychedelic Astral in your party: the road and the Jungle Shortcut are dark, and the UV pulse is what lights them. Halfway up the road a sacred cow called Lakshmi has been lying across it since Tuesday, and nobody is going to argue. You cannot get past her. Instead, take one of the two detours. Both leave the road near its south end and come back onto it near the north end, past the cow: West: the Jungle Shortcut. "It is not shorter." Longer, wilder, more trainers, and the lost tour group. East: the Roadside Shrine. A gate, a long walk, a marigold garden and a courtyard. The shrine's people have three side quests between them. Either way, at the top of the road go north into the Scooter Ditch.

A scooter jam in the dark, round a cow. Raver Jun at the north end: Glowkid Lv 15, Djembe-Monk Lv 15. Amber Vial (hidden): near the shrine turn-off in the south-east. Wild: Shadowcop, Mozzquito, Wooklet and Ketacrab (Lv 12–15), Sirenowl (Lv 13–15). Later, A Coconut for Lakshmi gets the cow off the road for good.

Five bends of dark jungle, climbing north. A stream with a single plank crosses it about halfway up, and Wook Basil watches the plank. At the bottom, Tour Leader Fergus of Gap Year Adventures has lost three backpackers. Beat each of them as you go and they walk back to him: The Lost Tour Group. Trainer Where Astrals Backpacker Saskia (the ukulele) Low down, west Snoozel Lv 14, Lassiblob Lv 15 Wook Basil At the north end of the plank Wooklet Lv 15, Mozzquito Lv 15, Sirenowl Lv 16 Dealer Raz Just past the stream, west Mozzquito, Wooklet, Shadowcop, all Lv 14 Coconut Wallah Pradeep His coconut grove, east Wooklet Lv 15, Chillem Lv 16, Ketacrab Lv 16 Backpacker Jonas (the hammock) Further up, west Tridog Lv 14, Wooklet Lv 15 Backpacker Tim (the opinions) Near the top, east Crabcake Lv 14, Mozzquito Lv 15, Glowkid Lv 15 Spinner Kavi Near the top, west Glowkid Lv 15, Nitroxide Lv 16 Items: a Mystery Powder (hidden) by Dealer Raz's spot just past the stream, 3 Rizla Papers in the middle bends, and 2 Tiger Balm near the top. Wild: Mozzquito, Wooklet and Tridog (Lv 12–15), Shroomba and Glowkid (Lv 13–15), Sirenowl (Lv 13–16).

Enter at the gate in the south. Guard Pinto and Flower Seller Meena stand at the gate, Baba Neem on the long walk north, then you reach the marigold garden, climb the steps into the courtyard with the shrine, and leave by the north side back onto the road. Trainer Where Astrals Guard Pinto The gate Shadowcop Lv 13, Sirenowl Lv 14 Flower Seller Meena The gate Shroomba Lv 14, Chillem Lv 15 Baba Neem The long walk Chillem Lv 15, Djembe-Monk Lv 15, Snoozel Lv 16 Pilgrim Devi The courtyard (she looks around in turns) Djembe-Monk Lv 15, Snoozel Lv 16 In the courtyard: Pujari Mohan explains that Lakshmi is not stubborn, she is offended: A Coconut for Lakshmi. The old woman finds fresh marigolds on the shrine every morning and has stopped asking where they come from: Flowers Before Dawn. Items: a Masala Chai in the west of the courtyard, an Amber Vial (hidden) in the marigold garden, and 2 Incense Sticks in the clearing north of the courtyard. Wild: Djembe-Monk, Snoozel, Lassiblob and Shadowcop (Lv 12–15), Chillem (Lv 13–15), Sirenowl (Lv 13–16).

A ditch full of half-sunk scooters with their indicators still blinking, and a stage in the middle with a captain's chair on it. A Chai Tent in the south-west, shut until Keta is beaten. A wook in the north-east knows the way on: "The sea goes to the lake, and the lake goes to the forest stage. You would need to float though." The north edge of the ditch is water. Trainer Astrals Mechanic Dinesh Ketacrab Lv 15, Crabcake Lv 15 Tourist Brenda Lobsterlad Lv 15 Both look around in turns rather than staring straight ahead. Items: a Warm Kingfisher in the north-west (the catalyst that turns a Crabcake into a Lobsterlad), 3 Rizla Papers in the south-east, and an Amber Vial (hidden) in the north-east. Wild: Ketacrab, Wooklet, Crabcake and Lassiblob (Lv 13–16), Nitroxide (Lv 14–16), Neighbula (Lv 15–16). Once you can float, the water holds Ketacrab (Lv 16–20) and Neighbula (Lv 18–20). tip Catch a Neighbula here if you can. It is Dissociative / Downer, takes almost nothing from Bummer moves, and will be exactly what you want against Baron Von Darkpsy. It is also a Dissociative, which you need for the Pink Flamingo Float.

"Ahoy... is the ditch moving, or is it me? It is me. I am the ditch." Astral Type Level Weak to Ketacrab Dissociative 16 Psychedelic, Organic Wooklet Organic / Dissociative 16 Psychedelic (four times), Organic Nitroxide Dissociative / Stimulant 15 Psychedelic, Dissociative Wonkrab Dissociative 18 Psychedelic, Organic His moment: "All hands! Sound the horns!" Scooter horns blare and the battle gets more intoxicated, which means more critical hits for both sides. Strategy: Psychedelic moves hit every one of his Astrals hard. Blottertot or Fractoad is ideal; a Glowkid or Shroomba works too. Organic moves are the other answer to the crabs. Do not bother with Stimulant or Bummer moves: Dissociative Astrals shrug them off. Nitroxide has the Burst ability: its first move after coming out hits twice as hard, and it pops at the end of its second turn whatever you do. Put something sturdy in front of it, or knock it out first. Keta's crabs have Dreamer: one attack in seven simply drifts past them. That is not bad luck, it is the ability. Reward: Rs 1500 and the Wonky Keychain.

Bass Drop Shove: with a Downer or Organic Astral in your party, you can shove subwoofers and passed-out wooks one tile. The one that matters is in the Flea Market's east gap: shove it and the way to the Back Alley and the Omelette Stall is open. Pushed things roll back when you leave, so you can never jam a gap for good. Three wristbands also means the festival timetable is on its way (next chapter). Rematch Keta offers a rematch once you have five wristbands: Ketacrab and Wooklet Lv 26, Nitroxide Lv 25, Wonkrab Lv 28.
Goal: beat Chef Raju for the Extra Cheese Stamp. Suggested level: 23–24. The Back Alley on the way is a gauntlet of seven trainers at Lv 19–22, so arrive ready for a long fight.
documents.s: 5. Chef Raju, the 5 AM Omelette Stall

documents.t: With three wristbands, the next time you walk into a new area Banyan jogs up waving a crumpled piece of paper. It is the Festival Timetable: a Sets page in your Fanny Pack and pink markers on the map. From now on sets play at fixed times, crowds fill the stage, and some Astrals only come out during a set. Time Set Where Brings out 6 to 8 AM Sunrise set Driftwood Shack Beach Neighbula (Lv 20–24); Banyan at the water 8 to 10 AM Ecstatic dance Tantric Yurt Chillem (Lv 20–24) 5 to 8 PM Night market Anjuna Flea Market Bribe-asaurus (Lv 20–24); the Night Market shop 6 to 8 PM Sponsored sunset Sunset Cliff Sirenowl (Lv 20–24) 10 PM to 1 AM Diabolo headline set Poi Pit Ravelord (Lv 20–24); Diabolo's rematch 2 to 5 AM Darkpsy hour Forest Stage Nitroxide (Lv 20–24) 5 to 7 AM The 5 AM rush Omelette Stall Omeletron (Lv 20–24) 9 PM to 3 AM Generator Disco Load-In Road (once its power is back) Glowkid (Lv 28–31) Any Chai Tent will now offer to let you sleep until a set starts. Two night trainers also appear: Night Owl Suki on the Sandy Trail and Insomniac Theo in the Flea Market (Duvetghast Lv 25, Snoozel Lv 26, Neighbula Lv 26), both from 10 PM to 5 AM. They are tough for now. tip The Night Market (Flea Market, 5 to 8 PM) has a night vendor selling Amber Vials, Mystery Powder, Warm Kingfisher, Banana Lassi, Neon Glowsticks, Electrolyte Sachets and the Glow Jacket. Mystery Powder turns a Glowkid into a Ravelord, which is a big upgrade at this point.

In the Flea Market, walk into the subwoofer in the east gap with a Downer or Organic Astral in your party: the Bass Drop Shove pushes it through. Behind it is the Flea Market Back Alley, and the Omelette Stall is on the far side.

Three dark yards of shipping containers joined by one-tile gaps. The first time you walk in, from either end, a shutter rattles down behind you. Constable Shah (hibiscus shirt, moustache stuck on crooked) explains that the exit is closed for a routine inspection. Of the air. Then he inspects your Astrals. Both ways out stay shut until you have beaten all seven of Team Undercover, in any order. There is no tent in here, so pace yourself and bring healing items. The quest log tracks it as The Back Alley. Trainer Astrals Constable Shah Shadowcop Lv 19, Mozzquito Lv 19 Undercover Tourist Gary Sirenowl Lv 19, Shadowcop Lv 20 Undercover Hippie River Chillem Lv 20, Mozzquito Lv 20 Undercover Sadhu Bhola Djembe-Monk Lv 20, Sirenowl Lv 21 Undercover Chai Wallah Sunil Lassiblob Lv 20, Shadowcop Lv 21 Undercover Juggler Prakash Glowkid Lv 21, Mozzquito Lv 21 Inspector Ashok Desai Shadowcop Lv 21, Dengoth Lv 22, Sirenowl Lv 22 Most of them are Bummer: Dissociative moves are the answer (Mozzquito and Dengoth take four times the damage), and Downer moves work on the pure Bummers. Inspector Desai also hands over a confiscated Mystery Powder. When the last one falls, a whistle blows, the moustaches come off, and the whole team files out through a door in a container: "WE WERE NEVER HERE." From then on the yards are full of people getting high. Item: 2 Water Bottles (hidden) in the far south-east corner.

"Open at 5 AM. It is always 5 AM." The stall is the second hub, in the east of the map. A Chai Tent in the east, shut until Raju is beaten. A local with a hint: "Raju's kitchen is all Organic and Downer. Stimulants cut through both." Exits: west back to the Alley, north through fairy lights to the Bamboo Thicket (Machete Hack), and south past banyan roots to the Backstage Container, which you cannot climb yet.

Chad is waiting just inside the west entrance, and he has been shopping. Your starter His team Ganjapod Selfiend Lv 16, Duvetghast Lv 17, Gurnagama Lv 18 Jawling Selfiend Lv 16, Duvetghast Lv 17, Fractoad Lv 18 Blottertot Selfiend Lv 16, Duvetghast Lv 17, Hashlump Lv 18 Selfiend (Stimulant / Bummer) takes four times the damage from Dissociative moves. Duvetghast is a Downer: Stimulant or Organic. His last Astral is your own starter's rival evolved, so plan the same way as on the Sandy Trail. He pays Rs 700, then walks off in a huff.
Trainer Astrals Wook Bodhi Wooklet Lv 17, Chillem Lv 17 Raver Pix Glowkid Lv 17, Mozzquito Lv 17, Djembe-Monk Lv 18

Day: Shroomba, Lassiblob, Chillem, Wooklet and Djembe-Monk (Lv 15–18), Snoozel (Lv 15–17). Night: Mozzquito, Sirenowl, Shadowcop and Chillem (Lv 15–18). During the 5 AM rush (5 to 7 AM): Omeletron (Lv 20–24).
Weighted Blanket: in the south-east corner. Masala Chai: in the south-west corner.

Astral Type Level Weak to Shroomba Organic / Psychedelic 20 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant Lassiblob Downer / Organic 20 Stimulant (four times), Organic Chillem Organic / Downer 21 Stimulant (four times), Organic Omeletron Organic / Psychedelic 23 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant His moment: "Special of the day! A second helping for my little one." His Astral heals 30% of its health. Strategy: Stimulant moves hit all four, and Lassiblob and Chillem take four times the damage. Jawling's line, a Glowkid or Ravelord, a Djembe-Monk or a Selfiend are all good. Bummer moves destroy Shroomba and Omeletron. A Mozzquito, Shadowcop or Sirenowl covers that half. Leave your Dissociative and Downer moves at home: Shroomba and Omeletron take only a quarter from Dissociative, and the two Downers resist both. Save a big hit for after his heal. Reward: Rs 2000, an Electrolyte Sachet and the Extra Cheese Stamp.

Pink Flamingo Float: with a Dissociative Astral in your party, you can walk on foam pits and shallow water. That opens two ways to the Forest Stage: north from the Scooter Ditch onto the Arabian Sea Shallows, or north from the Omelette Stall through the Bamboo Thicket, whose channel you can now float across. Four wristbands also satisfy the lifeguard on Driftwood Beach: Fishermen's Cove is open (next chapter). Rematch Raju offers a rematch once you have six wristbands: Shroomba and Lassiblob Lv 29, Chillem Lv 30, Omeletron Lv 32.
Goal: beat DJ Diabolo for the Hemp String Wristband. Suggested level: 11–12.

North of the Sandy Trail, the Poi Pit is a real dancefloor: a raised stage across the north with an LED wall, lasers and strobes, poi spinners at both edges, and a packed crowd in front of it. The crowd is an encounter area with a dancer on every tile, and there is no way round it: you have to wade through to reach the steps up onto the stage. The south end is the chill-out area: A Chai Tent (west) and a stall with the same stock as the Beach Stall. Both stay shut until Diabolo is beaten, so arrive healed. A hippie who explains that Diabolo will not even look at you unless you walk right up on stage and talk to him. A local with the most useful line in the early game: "Every type hits two others hard and bounces off two others. Stimulant flattens Organic and Downer." The Fire Spinner (east) has been spinning fire for six hours without a drink. Bring her two Coconut Waters for A Thirsty Spinner. The Beach Stall sells them for Rs 40.

Trainer Where Astrals Raver Miko Dancing on the west side of the crowd Glowkid Lv 6, Djembe-Monk Lv 6 Wook Sandy Dancing on the east side of the crowd Wooklet Lv 7 Both dance in place and look around in turns, so with good timing you can slip past. Fighting them is better practice.

Day: Djembe-Monk, Glowkid, Shroomba, Wooklet and Ketacrab (Lv 5–7). Blottertot (Lv 6–8) while Peaking. Night: Mozzquito (Lv 5–7), Glowkid (Lv 6–8), Shadowcop (Lv 6–7) and Tridog (Lv 5–7). During Diabolo's headline set (10 PM to 1 AM, once you have the timetable): Ravelord (Lv 20–24).

Tiger Balm: in the east of the chill-out area, near the Fire Spinner. 2 Watermelon Slices (hidden): in the south-east corner. Needs the UV pulse. 3 Rizla Papers: north of the stage, past the fairy lights. You can only get there after you win.

Climb the steps in the middle of the stage and talk to him. He has been mixing for nineteen hours and will not be interrupted by anything less than an astral clash. Astral Type Level Weak to Djembe-Monk Stimulant 8 Dissociative Wooklet Organic / Dissociative 8 Psychedelic (four times), Organic Glowkid Stimulant / Psychedelic 10 Bummer His moment: when his team drops to half its total health he shouts "THIS is the drop!", the music jumps to 176 BPM and his Astral gets faster. Strategy: A Ketacrab (Dissociative, from the beach or right here in the Pit) handles Djembe-Monk, and Djembe-Monk's Stimulant moves barely scratch it. Blottertot is the hero against Wooklet: Psychedelic moves hit it four times as hard. Glowkid is the real fight. It is the highest level and only Bummer moves hit it hard. A Tridog (Psychedelic / Bummer, from the Sandy Trail) or a night-time Shadowcop can help. Otherwise just bring levels and a few Coconut Waters. If you picked Ganjapod, it shrugs off Wooklet's Dissociative moves, but both Stimulant Astrals hit it hard. Lead with something else. Reward: Rs 600 and the Hemp String Wristband.

Machete Hack: with an Organic or Stimulant Astral in your party, you can now hack through fairy lights and bamboo. The first lights are right behind the stage: walk into them and you are through, on the road north to the Tantric Yurt. The Chai Tent and the stall open, and the Sandy Trail's ranger lets anyone through from now on. Rematch Diabolo offers a rematch once you have three wristbands, but only during his headline set: 10 PM to 1 AM, in the Pit. His team is then Djembe-Monk and Wooklet at Lv 18 and Glowkid at Lv 20. See After the credits.
Goal: beat Guru Svetlana for the Quartz Wristband. Suggested level: 15–16.

Hack through the fairy lights behind the Poi Pit's stage (Machete Hack) and walk north. You come out at the south end of the Tantric Yurt's grounds. The yurt itself is at the north end, with Svetlana on her cushion inside. The east exit leads to the Anjuna Flea Market, which you can visit straight away (see below).

"Shoes off. Ego off." A Chai Tent in the south-east, shut until Svetlana is beaten. A tourist who paid for a ten-day retreat and was told on day two that he was already enlightened. An acolyte inside the yurt, and, during the morning Ecstatic dance (8 to 10 AM, once you have the timetable), a gong player.
Trainer Astrals Yogi Anand Snoozel Lv 9, Lassiblob Lv 10 Hippie Sol Shroomba Lv 10, Tridog Lv 10 Acolyte Mira Glowkid Lv 11, Blottertot Lv 11

Day: Tridog (Lv 8–11), Shroomba (Lv 8–11), Glowkid (Lv 9–11), Lassiblob (Lv 9–11), Snoozel (Lv 8–10). Fractoad (Lv 10–12) while Peaking. Night: Mozzquito (Lv 9–11), Shadowcop (Lv 9–11), Tridog (Lv 9–12) and Sirenowl (Lv 11–12). During the Ecstatic dance (8 to 10 AM): Chillem (Lv 20–24).
2 Watermelon Slices: on the west side, by a lamp. Banana Lassi: in the north-east corner, beside the yurt. It is a catalyst: give it to a Snoozel and it becomes a Duvetghast on the spot.

The market east of the Yurt is the first hub and the best shop in the early game. It is worth a visit before the boss. The market vendor (north-west) sells everything a traveller needs: Ziploc Baggies and Rizla Papers, Coconut Water, Watermelon, Water Bottles, Electrolyte Sachets, Tiger Balm, Incense Sticks, Wraparound Shades, Earplugs, two catalysts (Warm Kingfisher, Banana Lassi), all four held items (Friendship Band, Neon Glowstick, Lucky Rupee, Steel Flask) and two outfits (Sequin Vest, Glow Jacket). The Sunrise Guesthouse (the door in the north-west): a bed for Rs 100, the tourist who lost the sandals you may already be carrying (The Lost Sandals), and Undercover Grunt Ravi (Shadowcop Lv 14, Mozzquito Lv 14). Beat him and he drops Undercover Memo 1. The market hippie tells you about Team Undercover, and asks you to bring him any of their paperwork. This starts Team Undercover's Plan. The collector (east) has never seen a proper Downer up close: A Collector's Eye. A Snoozel in your party is enough. Dealer Vik (south-east), a trainer: Shadowcop Lv 13, Mozzquito Lv 13. The Lassi Wallah explains catalysts: "Lassi for the sleepy ones, Kingfisher for the sunburned, powder for the glowing." A tuk-tuk driver who only takes press. Remember him. The market's other exits are all blocked for now: north by security ("Guru Svetlana decides who passes"), east by a subwoofer in the gap (Captain Keta's wristband), and south by padlocked VIP fences (Baron Von Darkpsy's). Market items: 2 Incense Sticks in the east, an Electrolyte Sachet in the west, and 2 Masala Chai (hidden) in the north-east, which need the UV pulse you are about to earn. Market wild Astrals: Lassiblob (Lv 11–14), Tridog (Lv 11–14), Djembe-Monk (Lv 11–14), Snoozel (Lv 11–13), Chillem (Lv 12–14) and Selfiend (Lv 13–14) by day; Shadowcop, Mozzquito, Sirenowl and Glowkid (around Lv 11–14) at night.
documents.s: Next door: the Anjuna Flea Market

documents.t: Astral Type Level Weak to Blottertot Psychedelic 12 Downer, Bummer Tridog Psychedelic / Bummer 12 Downer (four times), Bummer Fractoad Psychedelic 14 Downer, Bummer Her moment: at half health she chants, and the type chart turns upside down for three turns: "Now your strengths are your weaknesses, darling." Strategy: Bring Downers. A Snoozel (beach, trail, the Yurt itself) or a Lassiblob (the Yurt and the market) hits all three hard, and Psychedelic moves bounce off them. Bummer moves are the backup: Tridog, Shadowcop (at night) or Crabcake. When the chart flips, your Downer moves suddenly do a quarter or half damage. For those three turns, switch tactics: Dissociative moves now hit her Blottertot and Fractoad hard, and Stimulant or Organic moves hit Tridog hard. Or simply heal and wait the three turns out. Reward: Rs 1000 and the Quartz Wristband.

Blacklight UV Pulse: with a Psychedelic Astral in your party, dark places are lit up and hidden items appear. Go back for the Water Bottle in the Sandy Trail's tide pools, the 2 Watermelon Slices in the Poi Pit and the Masala Chai in the market. The market's security guard now lets you north: "The Guru vouched for you. Bring a light, it is black as a speaker cone up there." Rematch Svetlana offers a rematch once you have four wristbands: Blottertot and Tridog at Lv 22, Fractoad at Lv 24.
Goal: beat Influencer Chloe for the VIP Press Pass. Suggested level: 27–28.

Back to the Flea Market. At the south exit, walk into the padlocked VIP fence with a Stimulant Astral in your party: Jaw Grind chews straight through. South of it is the Dry Ice Corridor, and south of that the Sunset Cliff.

A maze of shipping containers and dry-ice foggers, indoors. The trainers here are a step up (Lv 25–27). Trainer Astrals Guard Dsouza Shadowcop Lv 25, Sirenowl Lv 25, Bribe-asaurus Lv 27 Dealer Moe Dengoth Lv 25, Nitroxide Lv 25, Mozzquito Lv 26 Influencer Jax Selfiend Lv 26, Glowkid Lv 26, Selfiend Lv 27

In the middle of the maze, a shape made of torch beams blocks the fog and rubs two fingers together. It wants Rs 500. Pay, and something small and sheepish drifts out of the light: a wild Shadowcop, Lv 25. Refuse (or be too broke), and it swells with indignation and grows a hat: a wild Bribe-asaurus, Lv 29. Either way it happens once, and you can try to bag what comes out. Items: 2 Amber Vials on the west side, a Masala Chai in the north-east corner, and 2 Electrolyte Sachets (hidden) in the north-west corner. Wild: Selfiend, Glowkid, Nitroxide and Shadowcop (Lv 25–28), Dengoth (Lv 26–28), and rarely Ravelord (Lv 30).

"This sunset is brought to you by a brand partner." A clifftop over the sea with a stage and a ring light, a crowd facing the sea with their phones out, and a fence along the west edge with a sign: LOOKING WEST, RS 2000. A Chai Tent in the south-west, shut until Chloe is beaten. The Sunset Watcher, sitting on a rock in the south-west, has watched the sunset through the gaps in the fence every evening. He will sit with you until 6 PM if you ask, which matters later for Sunraga. The Sunset Content Villa, the door in the north-west building. Inside: Assistant Pippa (Selfiend Lv 28, Lobsterlad Lv 28, Bongo Bishop Lv 29), Undercover Memo 2 and a Banana Lassi. Exits: north back to the Corridor, west down a path to Fishermen's Cove (free, any time), and east past banyan roots to the Load-In Road (needs the Ash Mark).
Influencer Bex near the villa: Selfiend Lv 26, Bongo Bishop Lv 26.

Wraparound Shades: at the west end, by the cliff path. While you carry them, trainers spot you from one tile less. Weighted Blanket: in the north-east corner. Neon Glowstick: up on a ledge in the north, behind a subwoofer. Shove it out of the way with the Bass Drop Shove, but think before you push: shoved straight in, it jams. If that happens, leave the cliff and come back, because pushed things roll back when you leave. Neon Glowstick: out over the sea in the south-east, on the stairs of light that only exist while your ego is gone. If you come down while you are standing out there, you wash up on Driftwood Beach.
Selfiend (Lv 23–25), Lobsterlad, Bongo Bishop, Tridog, Nitroxide and Neighbula (Lv 23–25). During the Sponsored sunset (6 to 8 PM): Sirenowl (Lv 20–24).

"Hi guys! So today we are at the most EXCLUSIVE sunset in Goa..." Astral Type Level Weak to Selfiend Stimulant / Bummer 25 Dissociative (four times) Gurnagama Stimulant 25 Dissociative Bongo Bishop Stimulant 26 Dissociative Ravelord Stimulant / Psychedelic 26 Bummer Her moment: "Chat is going WILD." She plays to her followers and her Astral gets +1 Fractal power and +1 Vibe attack. Strategy: Her whole team is Stimulant. Dissociative moves take three of them apart, and Selfiend takes four times the damage. Neighbula, Wonkrab, Wooklet or Grand Wook, or your Hoffmanite later. Ravelord is the exception: only Bummer moves hit it hard. Sirenowl, Dengoth or Bribe-asaurus. Organic and Downer Astrals take extra damage from Stimulant moves. Keep Chillem and friends away from this stage. Reward: Rs 3200 and the VIP Press Pass.

Share Taxi Tuk-Tuk: open the Map tab and choose a Chai Tent you have rested at, and a tuk-tuk takes you there, with a short ride over the night road. It does not run from the Mainstage Temple. The driver at the Flea Market is suddenly very friendly. The sadhu guarding the Sadhu Cave's mouth on the Sea Shallows now lets you in: "A press pass. Go in. Mind your head, and your sense of self." Rematch Chloe offers a rematch once you have all eight wristbands: Selfiend and Gurnagama Lv 37, Bongo Bishop Lv 38, Ravelord Lv 40.
Goal: get a starter from Professor Banyan, catch a second Astral, and walk north to the Poi Pit. Suggested level by the end: 6–7.
documents.s: 1. Driftwood Beach and the Sandy Trail

documents.t: The game opens in a dream. You are lying on warm sand at 4 PM and a white-bearded face with pupils like dinner plates is hanging over you. He explains the basics while you are out cold: Astrals, battling, bagging, Hydration and Serotonin, the blotter in your fanny pack, and the eight Wristbands of Enlightenment that get you in to see the VIP Shaman Council. He asks who you are (Moonbeam, Dave or Ziggy) and lets you ask him one question. None of the answers change anything. "Where are my shoes?" gets the most honest reply. Then you wake up for real, face-down in the sand. Your backpack, your shoes and your passport are gone. In their place: a fanny pack, half a bottle of warm coconut water and a Glowing Blotter.

Walk over to the old man by the shack. Professor Banyan came to Goa in 1994 for two weeks. He tells you the Council has your passport, and that you need all eight wristbands to get in. Then he offers you one of the three Astrals from his stash, all at level 5. Starter Type Ability Evolves In short Ganjapod Organic Second Wind Hashlump at 16, Charagolem (Organic / Downer) at 36 "A sleepy coconut. Slow, sturdy, and it heals itself on the couch." Jawling Stimulant Overdrive Gurnagama at 16, Amphetadragon (Stimulant / Bummer) at 36 "A gecko that never stops talking. Fast and fragile." Blottertot Psychedelic Clear Head Fractoad at 16, Hoffmanite (Psychedelic / Dissociative) at 36 "A paper frog. Strange powers, and it bends the rules." Whichever you pick, your rival turns up with the one that was meant to beat it. Pick Ganjapod and he brings a Jawling, whose Stimulant moves hit Organic Astrals twice as hard: that is the toughest start of the three. The two starters you did not pick are not gone for good: they hide in the early zones and only show themselves while you are Peaking (see Peak Experience). Banyan also gives you 5 Ziploc Baggies and 3 Coconut Water, explains the four levels of high (Microdose, Come-up, Peaking and Ego gone), and takes down the festival tape across the beach path. Two tips from him worth remembering: hold B to run, and do not stand still too long with the blotter in your bag, or you will start licking it out of boredom.

The beach is your home base for the whole game. Chai Tent (east side): Chai Mama heals everything and keeps your stash. Banyan's Shack (the door in the north-west): his hammock heals and becomes your whiteout point. The diary on the table gives you a Masala Chai the first time you read it, and there is a pickup of 2 Water Bottles inside. Beach Stall (the vendor in the middle): Ziploc Baggies, Coconut Water, Water Bottles, Tiger Balm, and two outfits (Tie-Dye Shirt, Cotton Kurta). Water Bottle on the sand in the south-east, by the waterline. The Crab Raver on the west of the beach starts The Crab Rave. It takes the whole game to finish, so just say hello for now. While you are Peaking, a Glowing Stranger stands on the sand to the east. Sober, you cannot see them at all. The first time they give you 2 Amber Vials. The lifeguard on the rocks at the east end turns you back: Fishermen's Cove is round there, but he wants to see four wristbands first. Wild Astrals in the incense clouds: Crabcake (Lv 2–3), Ketacrab (Lv 2–4) and Snoozel (Lv 2–3). While Peaking, Ganjapod (Lv 3–4) turns up too. tip Catch something here. Ketacrab is a Dissociative crab, the one type DJ Diabolo's Djembe-Monk is weak to. Wear one down, then throw a baggie.

Head north up the beach path. The Sandy Trail winds north for a good while: South of the creek: tide pools in the west and a drum circle round a bonfire in the east, with a yogi sitting on the logs. Four incense clouds to catch in. The creek: one plank bridge, and the Fire-Spinner watches the far end of it, so you cannot sneak past her. North of the creek: dunes, a surfboard stuck in the sand, more incense, and a funnel of dunes and palms leading up to the Poi Pit. Your rival watches the funnel. The north exit: Ranger Asha.

If you are carrying only one Astral, the ranger will not let you through: "Diabolo's crowd will eat you alive. Bag one more in the incense first." Talk to her and she gives you 3 Ziploc Baggies, once. With two Astrals she waves you on, and once Diabolo is beaten the way is always open.

Trainer Where Astrals Beach Bum Rick Right at the start of the trail Crabcake Lv 3 Juggler Dev West of the path, south of the creek Djembe-Monk Lv 3 Drummer Kofi The drum circle in the east (optional) Djembe-Monk Lv 4, Tridog Lv 4 Fire-Spinner Lola Just over the plank bridge Crabcake Lv 3, Snoozel Lv 4 Astra-Zero The funnel below the Poi Pit His starter, Lv 5 (see below) Later in the game, once you have the Festival Timetable, Night Owl Suki appears on the trail between 10 PM and 5 AM with a Glowkid (Lv 24) and a Sirenowl (Lv 25). Ignore her for now: she is not here yet.

Day: Crabcake, Djembe-Monk, Tridog and Snoozel (Lv 3–5), Shroomba (Lv 4–5). Jawling (Lv 4–6) while Peaking. Night (7 PM to 6 AM): Mozzquito (Lv 3–5), Tridog (Lv 4–6), Snoozel (Lv 3–5) and Shadowcop (Lv 4–5).

Watermelon Slice: by the drum circle in the south-east. Water Bottle (hidden): in the tide pools in the south-west. Hidden items only show once you have the Quartz Wristband and a Psychedelic Astral; come back for it later. 2 Ziploc Baggies: on the far west edge, north of the creek. Lost Sandals: in the east, north of the creek. They belong to a tourist at the Sunrise Guesthouse (The Lost Sandals). Pick them up now and hand them in when you reach the Flea Market. Ziploc Baggie: in the dunes in the north-east.

The guy from the seat next to you on the charter flight now calls himself Astra-Zero. Brand-new harem pants, a trust fund and a store-bought Astral picked to beat yours. He blocks the funnel on the way to the Poi Pit and you cannot walk round him. Your starter His Astral Ganjapod Jawling, Lv 5 (Stimulant) Jawling Blottertot, Lv 5 (Psychedelic) Blottertot Ganjapod, Lv 5 (Organic) He pays Rs 250. With Ganjapod, switch in your second catch if Jawling is hurting you; with Blottertot, your Psychedelic moves hit his Ganjapod twice as hard. Then go north into the Poi Pit.

Goal: cross the Mainstage crowd, beat the Front Row, and get yourself crowd-surfed onto the temple. Suggested level: 40–41. "Between the Backstage and the Mainstage: ten thousand people, and every one of them is in your way." This is the victory road. It runs a long way south from the Backstage's velvet rope to the stage at the bottom, and it is built in bands: a chill-out ring at the top, then three bands of dancing lanes, with packed crowds and trainers in between. There is a Chai Tent at the top, so you can always walk back up to heal.

The lanes are rows of dancers. With every step you take, each row's dancers move one tile along it, in groups with gaps. Some rows go faster, some slower, some the other way. You cannot walk into a dancer. Try, and you wait a beat while the row moves on, so you can never be boxed in. Nobody ever dances onto the tile you are standing on. So: step into a gap, watch the next row, step again. "Patience is a dance move too." The packed crowds between the lanes are encounter areas, like the Poi Pit's.

The top of the field, just south of the Backstage. The welfare tent in the north-west, with a Chai Tent. Ziggy, by the welfare tent, has lost her friend Noor in the crowd: Lost in the Crowd. The Merch Stall in the north-east: Amber Vials, Rizla Papers, Weighted Blankets, Electrolyte Sachets, the Glow Jacket and the Sequin Vest. "Official merch! Unofficial merch! The difference is the price and nothing else." A sign explaining the lanes.

Every boss you beat has a superfan down here, and each has a line about their hero. They stand in the open spaces between the lanes. Trainer Where Astrals Poi Superfan Rahul The Outer Ring, east Gurnagama Lv 36, Ravelord Lv 37 Breathwork Superfan Ilse Below the first lanes, west Duvetghast Lv 36, Lassiblob Lv 37, Snoozel Lv 37 Ditch Superfan Mo Below the first lanes, east Wonkrab Lv 37, Neighbula Lv 37, Hoffmanite Lv 38 Omelette Superfan Gita In the west crowd, middle section Omeletron Lv 37, Shroomba Lv 37, Charagolem Lv 38 Darkpsy Superfan Vlad In the east crowd, middle section Omnihound Lv 37, Sirenowl Lv 38 Influencer Superfan Bella Below the second lanes, in the middle (looks around) Selfiend Lv 38, Mozzquito Lv 37, Dengoth Lv 38 Smoke Superfan Om By the light towers, west Grand Wook Lv 38, Hoffmanite Lv 38, Chillem Lv 38 VIP Superfan Brent By the light towers, east Bribe-asaurus Lv 38, Amphetadragon Lv 39

Between the first and second bands of lanes, Marta's sound desk sits in its pen in the middle of the field, with packed crowds either side. Marta mixes the Mainstage, and she explains how it works: "The Council only let in people the crowd carries. There is no stairway, no guest list. There is the crowd, and the crowd decides." Beat the Front Row at the barrier and the crowd will lift you.
Between the second and third bands. Noor is here, in the east, dancing on exactly the spot she promised not to leave.

At the bottom, past the third band of lanes, is the barrier in front of the stage. A one-tile run leads to the only gap in it, and the Front Row stand guard in alcoves looking into the run. They have been here since the gates opened. Trainer Astrals Front Row Kiki Ravelord Lv 39, Fractoad Lv 39, Omnihound Lv 40 Front Row Dex Amphetadragon Lv 39, Grand Wook Lv 39, Hoffmanite Lv 40 Kiki's team is Psychedelic at heart: Bummer moves hit Ravelord and Fractoad, and Downer moves hit Fractoad and Omnihound (four times). Dex is mixed: Dissociative moves hit Amphetadragon four times as hard; Psychedelic moves hit Grand Wook four times and Hoffmanite twice; Organic and Downer moves also hit Hoffmanite. A security guard at the west end of the front explains the side gate: it is the temple's back stairs. "You can come out this way. You cannot go in this way. Going in is up to the crowd."

Water Bottle x3: east side, middle section, just below the first lanes. Warm Kingfisher: in a clearing in the west crowd, middle section. 2 Amber Vials: far west edge, middle section. Masala Chai (hidden): in the clearing in the east crowd, just beside Darkpsy Superfan Vlad. 2 Weighted Blankets: far west edge, by the light towers. 2 Electrolyte Sachets: east side, by the light towers, right next to Noor. 2 Tiger Balm: far east edge at the front, below the third lanes.

The packed crowds hold the strongest wild Astrals in the game: Ravelord, Omnihound, Grand Wook and Selfiend (Lv 35–38), Amphetadragon and Charagolem (Lv 36–38), and Dengoth (Lv 35–37). This is the only place to catch a wild Amphetadragon or Charagolem.

Until both of the Front Row are beaten, the crowd will not lift you: "The Front Row are still watching you, arms folded. The crowd takes its cue from them." Beat Kiki and Dex, heal at the welfare tent if you need to, and step into the gap in the barrier. Somebody behind you shouts your name. Then everybody does. A hundred hands lift you off your feet and pass you forward over the heads (somebody steals one of your sandals; it is worth it), and the last row throws you, quite hard, up over the lip of the stage. After that, coming back through the gap gives you a short version: the crowd knows you now, and passes you up "like a parcel". The temple's back stairs bring you out at the side gate here, so you can come back down to heal or shop at any time.
Goal: climb the ziggurat past the Four-on-the-Floor and your rival, and face the VIP Shaman Council. Suggested level: 42–44.

You land on warm stone. Behind the stage, the Mainstage Temple goes up in terraces into the dark. On the first terrace a kick drum starts; on the second, a bassline; on the third, a hi-hat ticking like a clock; on the fourth, a melody you feel you have always known. At the very top, three figures stand against the stars and look down at you. "Climb, then. Everybody wants to be at the top. Very few want to climb." The temple is a terraced ziggurat: a plaza at the foot, then five terraces, each narrower and higher than the last, with the Council on the summit. Each terrace's stair is one tile wide, and someone stands at the top of every stair. Nobody can walk round them. There are no wild Astrals here, and no tuk-tuk will take you away from it.

A Chai Tent in the west. It works until your first fight with the Four. Once you have beaten one of them, Chai Mama refuses until you have beaten all four: "You started. Finish, then sit, and I will pour." The Water Auntie next to it. The first time you talk to her on a climb, she heals your whole party ("you look like a raisin. Drink. All of you."). After that her chai is finished, but her water jug never is: she refills your Astrals' Hydration as often as you like. A roadie in the east sums up what is coming: "Kick, bass, hat, lead. Heavy, wobbly, fast, clever. Then whoever is sulking in the last doorway." Items: 3 Masala Chai in the east and 2 Weighted Blankets in the south-west corner. The back stairs at the foot of the plaza lead down to the Last Dancefloor's side gate. The Four are one climb If you white out partway up, the climb starts over: all four are back at their posts and the Water Auntie's chai is full again. Stock up on Masala Chai, Weighted Blankets and Electrolyte Sachets before your first fight (the Backstage Bar and the Merch Stall sell them), and rest at the plaza tent before you start. When you beat one of the Four, they walk up through their door and stand aside on the next terrace, cheering you on.

The first terrace: speaker stacks and a kick-drum pulse. "First of the Four-on-the-Floor. I am the kick drum..." Astral Type Level Weak to Duvetghast Downer 36 Stimulant, Organic Chillem Organic / Downer 36 Stimulant (four times), Organic Lassiblob Downer / Organic 37 Stimulant (four times), Organic Grand Wook Organic / Dissociative 37 Psychedelic (four times), Organic Charagolem Organic / Downer 39 Stimulant (four times), Organic Her moment: "BOOM! And now the kick comes in for real!" Her Astral's Vibe attack goes up two stages. Strategy: heavy and slow. A Stimulant Astral (Amphetadragon, Ravelord, Bongo Bishop) tears through four of the five; keep a Psychedelic one for Grand Wook. After her moment her physical hits get much stronger, so finish fast or switch to an Astral with high Ego defence.

The second terrace: subwoofers and a rumble you feel in your feet. "Second. I am the bassline..." Astral Type Level Weak to Wonkrab Dissociative 37 Psychedelic, Organic Neighbula Dissociative / Downer 37 Organic (four times) Nitroxide Dissociative / Stimulant 38 Psychedelic, Dissociative Grand Wook Organic / Dissociative 38 Psychedelic (four times), Organic Hoffmanite Psychedelic / Dissociative 39 Psychedelic, Organic, Downer His moment: "Feel the floor? That is my bass. It does not stop." His Astral's Ego defence and Groundedness go up one stage each. Strategy: wobbly and Dissociative through and through. Psychedelic moves hit four of the five (Grand Wook four times); Organic moves hit four too (Neighbula four times). A Mandalord, if you have one, is made for this. Stimulant and Bummer moves bounce off. Nitroxide pops after its second turn; do not waste your best Astral on its first, doubled hit.

The third terrace: strobes ticking on the off-beat. "Third-third-third! I am the hi-hat..." Astral Type Level Weak to Bongo Bishop Stimulant 38 Dissociative Dengoth Bummer / Stimulant 38 Dissociative (four times) Selfiend Stimulant / Bummer 39 Dissociative (four times) Ravelord Stimulant / Psychedelic 39 Bummer Amphetadragon Stimulant / Bummer 40 Dissociative (four times) Her moment: "Double time! Tss-tss-tss-tss!" Her Astral gets two stages faster. Strategy: fast. Dissociative moves hit four of the five, three of them four times as hard: Hoffmanite, Grand Wook, Neighbula or Wonkrab. Keep a Bummer Astral for Ravelord. Organic Astrals have a terrible time here.

The fourth terrace: banners and drifting notes. "Fourth. I am the lead line..." Astral Type Level Weak to Omnihound Psychedelic / Bummer 39 Downer (four times), Bummer Sirenowl Bummer 39 Dissociative, Downer Omeletron Organic / Psychedelic 39 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant Bribe-asaurus Bummer 39 Dissociative, Downer Hoffmanite Psychedelic / Dissociative 40 Psychedelic, Organic, Downer Mandalord Psychedelic / Organic 41 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant Her moment: "And now, the melody you have been waiting for." Her Astral's Fractal power goes up two stages. Strategy: clever, with six Astrals and a Mandalord of her own. Downer moves hit four of the six (Omnihound four times); Bummer moves hit Omnihound, and Omeletron and Mandalord four times. A Duvetghast plus a Bummer Astral (Bribe-asaurus, Sirenowl, Amphetadragon) covers almost everything. Her moment boosts astral attacks, so an Astral with high Groundedness helps.

The fifth terrace, the last doorway before the summit. "You. Of course it is you." YOUR RIVAL · ASTRA-ZERO · "The very well dressed ego." Your starter His team Ganjapod Selfiend Lv 39, Duvetghast Lv 39, Omnihound Lv 40, Ravelord Lv 40, Grand Wook Lv 41, Amphetadragon Lv 43 Jawling Selfiend Lv 39, Duvetghast Lv 39, Omnihound Lv 40, Ravelord Lv 40, Grand Wook Lv 41, Hoffmanite Lv 43 Blottertot Selfiend Lv 39, Duvetghast Lv 39, Omnihound Lv 40, Ravelord Lv 40, Grand Wook Lv 41, Charagolem Lv 43 Strategy: Selfiend: Dissociative (four times). Duvetghast: Stimulant or Organic. Omnihound: Downer (four times). Ravelord: Bummer. Grand Wook: Psychedelic (four times). His ace is your starter's rival, fully evolved: Amphetadragon takes four times the damage from Dissociative moves; Hoffmanite is weak to Psychedelic, Organic and Downer; Charagolem takes four times the damage from Stimulant moves. He pays Rs 8000, then stands aside on the Council's terrace. "Whatever. Go on, then. They are waiting. ...Good luck, I guess. Do not tell anyone I said that."

The summit, in gold light. The Elder, the Seer and the Bead-Beard hum in harmony. This is not a fight. "So. The barefoot one. Eight wristbands, four terraces, and one very well dressed ego, all behind you." They tell you the truth about your passport, which you may already suspect: it fell out of your pocket on the beach, and they kept it safe. They could have just handed it back, but then you would have gone home on Tuesday with a clean shirt and no stories. They give you the Passport. Your return flight left six days ago. Or it leaves tomorrow. Time is not their department. Then you choose: Go home: "A sensible choice. Banyan made the same one in 1994. He is still packing." Two more weeks: "Two more weeks. Yes. That is what they all say. That is what we said." Either way the credits roll, then the end card. You wake up on Driftwood Beach, healed, next to Banyan: "Ah, you are back. With a passport! Put it somewhere safe. Not too safe." The festival goes on, your Journal still has blank pages, and, he adds, there is something in the Sadhu Cave that has been watching for a very long time. On to After the credits.
Goal: beat the Promoter for the All-Access Hologram. Suggested level: 37–38. He brings six Astrals.

Two ways in, both opened by the Ash Mark's Banyan Root Climb: The short way: from the Omelette Stall, climb down the roots at the south exit. You arrive at the Backstage's north door. The Omelette Stall's Chai Tent is the nearest place to heal, just one screen away. The long way: from the Sunset Cliff, climb the roots at the east exit onto the Load-In Road, and follow it east to the Backstage's west door. Worth doing once: it has eight trainers, a side quest and a shop.

The festival's service road, from the Sunset Cliff to the Backstage. A truck park in the north (lorries nose to tail, flight cases, a container stack, light towers), the road itself through the middle with cable ramps and a security checkpoint, the lighting store in the south-west (a maze of flight cases), a fenced generator yard in the south, and a crew catering corner in the south-east, where Chef Bruno sells Masala Chai, Banana Lassi, Watermelon, Coconut Water and Water Bottles. All three generators are dead, and front-of-house engineer Deepak thinks somebody read a memo about cutting the power: Power Cut. Get them running and the crew throw the Generator Disco in the truck park every night from 9 PM to 3 AM. Trainer Astrals Rigger Tomasz Bribe-asaurus Lv 28, Dengoth Lv 28, Shadowcop Lv 29 Lighting Tech Ines Glowkid Lv 28, Selfiend Lv 29 Forklift Fatima Charagolem Lv 28, Bribe-asaurus Lv 29 Roadie Big Steve Grand Wook Lv 29, Bongo Bishop Lv 29 Runner Jess Nitroxide Lv 28, Mozzquito Lv 29, Selfiend Lv 29 Security Ramesh Shadowcop Lv 29, Bribe-asaurus Lv 29 Line Cook Pilar Omeletron Lv 29, Lassiblob Lv 29, Shroomba Lv 30 Bottler Gunther Bribe-asaurus Lv 30, Shadowcop Lv 30, Dengoth Lv 31 Bottler Gunther is the "maintenance man" crouched by the third generator with a hose. Several of the others look around in turns. Items: Banana Lassi: in the truck park in the north-west, between flight cases. 2 Amber Vials: in the far north-east, behind the containers. Jerrycan: deep in the lighting store maze. Generator two needs it. 2 Tiger Balm: in the lighting store maze. Weighted Blanket: inside the generator yard. 2 Electrolyte Sachets (hidden): in the far south-east corner. Wild: Selfiend, Bribe-asaurus, Dengoth and Bongo Bishop (Lv 27–30), Shadowcop (Lv 28–30), Nitroxide and Mozzquito (Lv 27–29). During the Generator Disco: Glowkid (Lv 28–31).

"If you can read this you should not be here." The Promoter sits in the big chair at the north of the main hall, behind a velvet rope, with a table of cash and a stack of speakers that shakes. The Backstage Bar (south-east) sells Amber Vials, Rizla Papers, Masala Chai, Watermelon, Electrolyte Sachets, Tiger Balm, Weighted Blankets and Mystery Powder, at "artist prices. You are not an artist, so double." It stays shut until the Promoter is beaten. There is no Chai Tent. The Promoter's place; nobody rests here. A roadie warns you: "The Promoter carries one of everything. No type will save you. Bring a full party and a lot of water." The Green Room, the door in the north wall of the main hall (see below). The velvet rope across the south exit, and a man with a clipboard: "All-Access Hologram or nothing." Trainer Astrals Bouncer Tiny Bribe-asaurus Lv 31, Duvetghast Lv 31, Dengoth Lv 32 Bouncer Mountain Lobsterlad Lv 32, Wonkrab Lv 32, Bribe-asaurus Lv 33 Items: 3 Amber Vials in the north-east corner, 2 Masala Chai in the south-west, and 2 Electrolyte Sachets (hidden) among the flight cases in the east. Wild: Selfiend, Ravelord, Bribe-asaurus, Dengoth, Duvetghast and Bongo Bishop (Lv 32–34).

Two of Team Undercover's Bottlers guard the room where the dopamine is bottled: Bottler Kiran: Dengoth Lv 33, Bribe-asaurus Lv 34. Bottler Meera: Selfiend Lv 34, Ravelord Lv 35. Undercover Memo 3 is in the north-west corner, walled off behind two subwoofers. You need the Bass Drop Shove, and the two must be moved in the right order: if you get it wrong, step out and back in and they reset. 2 Amber Vials wait in the same nook.

If you have been collecting the memos, this is where the story comes together: Memo 1: from Undercover Grunt Ravi in the Sunrise Guesthouse (chapter 3). "Phase 1: buy every guesthouse bed in Anjuna. Phase 2: charge for sleep. Phase 3: charge for dreams." Memo 2: in the Sunset Content Villa on the cliff (chapter 7). "Influencers have fenced off the sunset. Looking west now costs Rs 2000." Memo 3: here in the Green Room. "When the bottles are full, the Promoter cuts the power to every free party in Goa. Only the Mainstage stays loud. Shred after reading." Take all three to the hippie at the Flea Market. He pins copies in every Chai Tent from here to Arambol and gives you Rs 2000 and a Mystery Powder. The fence on the cliff comes down, and the sunset is free again: that opens The Freed Sunset, the hunt for Sunraga. Then he warns you: their head of security, Sergeant Baksheesh, has seen the copies and is on his way to the Sunset Cliff. He waits on the cliff, by the east exit. "I had a permit. I wrote it myself." Astral Type Level Weak to Bribe-asaurus Bummer 33 Dissociative, Downer Sirenowl Bummer 34 Dissociative, Downer Dengoth Bummer / Stimulant 34 Dissociative (four times) Shadowcop Bummer 34 Dissociative, Downer Bribe-asaurus Bummer 35 Dissociative, Downer Every one of them is Bummer, so Dissociative moves win this, with Downer moves as backup. The third memo is only reachable after Baba Smoke, so the Sergeant brings a team to match (since 1.3.0): treat him like a boss and heal first. He pays Rs 3400, and that closes Team Undercover's Plan for good.
documents.s: Team Undercover's Plan, and Sergeant Baksheesh

documents.t: "Seven wristbands. Barefoot. No passport..." Astral Type Level Weak to Bribe-asaurus Bummer 35 Dissociative, Downer Ravelord Stimulant / Psychedelic 35 Bummer Duvetghast Downer 35 Stimulant, Organic Wonkrab Dissociative 36 Psychedelic, Organic Omeletron Organic / Psychedelic 36 Bummer (four times), Psychedelic, Stimulant Amphetadragon Stimulant / Bummer 37 Dissociative (four times) His moment: "Security!
